## Duplicate Seller Leads in Salesforce: Rules That Work
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-duplicate-sellers.html

Duplicate seller leads in Salesforce: rules that catch them without losing leads
A home-buying company creates duplicates faster than almost any other kind of business. The same owner gets six mailers and calls from a different phone each time, cold-call lists get re-imported every month, and a seller who went quiet in March calls a new number in September. Each copy inflates your lead count, splits the history and can put two reps on the same seller. This guide is for ops leads and acquisitions managers on Salesforce: how duplicate management actually works, where it quietly doesn't, and the setup I'd use for an investor team.
Match sellers on a cleaned phone number, email and property address, not on name and company. Set duplicate rules to alert people who type records in, but never to block records your integrations and web forms create, because a blocked web form is a lost seller. Remember that duplicate rules don't run in some cases, including records saved together in one import, so de-duplicate lists before you load them. When a known seller comes back, route them to their original owner and keep the history on one record.
Why do investor CRMs fill up with duplicates?
Sellers call from different numbers. A landline for the first mailer, a cell for the second, a spouse's phone for the third.
Lists overlap. Absentee owners, pre-foreclosures, tax delinquent, probate: the same owner shows up on several lists, often with several skip-traced numbers.
Lists get re-imported. Cold-calling teams load a fresh list every month, and last month's sellers come in again.
Many doors in. Phone, web form, PPC form, text reply, a cold caller's handoff, a referral. Each one can create a record.
Properties have more than one owner. Heirs, ex-spouses and co-owners can each become a lead for the same house.
What do duplicates cost you?
Bad numbers. Lead counts go up, so cost per lead looks better than it is, and conversion rates look worse.
Two reps, one seller. The seller gets two calls and two different offers, and the reps argue about who owns the deal.
Lost history. The rep calling the new record doesn't see that the seller turned down an offer in the spring, or what their real reason for selling was.
Compliance risk. A seller who opted out on one record can still get texts from the automation running on the other copy.
That last one is the one I'd fix first. Whatever else you do, an opt-out or Do Not Call flag on any copy should count for the person.
How does Salesforce catch duplicates?
Two pieces work together:
Matching rules define what "the same" means: which fields to compare and how strictly. Salesforce's standard lead matching rule compares name, company, email and phone with fuzzy matching.
Duplicate rules decide what happens when a match is found: allow the save with an alert, block it, and whether to log it to a report.
The standard rule is built for B2B sales, where a company name means something. Seller leads usually have no company, and the name is often just what the seller said on the phone. That's why investor orgs need their own matching rules, built around what actually identifies a seller: phone, email and the property.
Limits worth knowing: up to five active duplicate rules per object, up to three matching rules in one duplicate rule, and up to five active matching rules per object. A lead duplicate rule can also compare new leads against existing contacts, which matters if you convert leads.
Where do duplicate rules not run?
This is the part that catches people out. According to Salesforce, duplicate rules don't run when:
Records are created with Quick Create.
Leads are converted, unless the "Use Apex Lead Convert" setting is on.
Records are restored from the Recycle Bin.
Records are created by Lightning Sync or Einstein Activity Capture.
Records are merged by hand.
And a few behaviors that surprise people:
Records saved at the same time aren't compared with each other. If one import file contains the same seller twice, both get created.
On edits, a rule only runs when an edited field is in the matching rule. Changing a seller's phone number triggers it. Changing their motivation doesn't.
Imports and API connections can't show an alert. A rule that would show a person a warning can make an import or integration fail instead. That's what's behind an import that errors with DUPLICATES_DETECTED.
The setup I'd use for an investor team
1. Clean the keys before matching
Phone numbers arrive as (614) 555-0100, 614.555.0100 and +16145550100. Add a field that stores the number as digits only, filled by a before-save Flow, and match on that. Do the same for the property address: one cleaned street field, so "123 N Main St" and "123 North Main Street" have a chance of matching.
2. Match on what identifies a seller
Cleaned phone, exact match.
Email, exact match.
Cleaned property street plus zip code.
Use them as separate conditions (phone OR email OR property), not all at once, because a returning seller rarely matches on everything.
3. Alert people, never block integrations
Who creates the record | What the rule should do | Why
A rep or VA typing it in | Allow, with an alert that shows the existing record | They can open the existing seller instead of creating a new one
Web forms, the dialer, texting tools, Zapier | Allow and report, then let a Flow handle it | A blocked record from an integration is a lost lead, and nobody sees the error
List imports | De-duplicate before loading (see below) | Rules don't compare records in the same file
4. Report every match
Turn on reporting in the duplicate rule, so every match is logged. A weekly look at the duplicate report tells you which door is creating them, which is usually more useful than cleaning them up one by one.
5. Make opt-outs follow the person
When a match is found, copy any opt-out or Do Not Call flag to every matching record, and stop automations on all of them.
How should you handle list imports?
If your team cold calls, lists are likely your biggest source of duplicates, so this is where to be strict:
De-duplicate the file itself before import, on phone and property address. Salesforce won't compare rows in the same file with each other.
Check the file against Salesforce on the same keys, and split it into new sellers and sellers you already have.
Load only the new ones as new leads. For existing sellers, update the record or add them to the new campaign, so their history stays in one place.
Tag every row with the list and the campaign , so you can tell later which list produced the deal.
Your list provider or skip-tracing tool may do the first step for you. The second step is the easy one to skip.
How should you merge duplicates?
In Salesforce you can merge up to three leads at a time, and the person merging needs Delete permission on leads. Keep that permission with ops or an admin, not every rep.
Pick the surviving record on purpose: usually the oldest one with the most activity, so the seller's history stays together.
Decide ahead of time which lead source wins. If the seller first came from a mailer and called back from a PPC ad, your attribution rule should decide, not whoever happens to merge. My take on that is in which campaign gets credit .
Check opt-outs and Do Not Call on every record before you merge, and keep the strictest one.
Do it on a schedule. A weekly 20-minute merge session beats a yearly clean-up of thousands of records.
What should happen when a seller comes back?
A seller who went quiet and then calls again is one of the best leads you'll get, and one of the easiest to mishandle. The right behavior:
The call or form matches the existing seller on phone, email or property.
Instead of a new lead going into round robin, the existing record is updated and reopened.
The original owner gets a notification that their seller is back, with the new source.
If the original owner has left, the seller goes to the queue with their history attached.
Duplicate handling that keeps the history and notifies the original owner is part of the setup I run for a two-market home-buying company in Ohio.
To bring quiet sellers back on purpose rather than waiting for them to call, see reactivating dead seller leads .
Questions
Why does Salesforce still let duplicate leads through?
Usually because the matching rule doesn't fit seller data (it relies on name and company), the record came in a way duplicate rules don't cover (such as Quick Create, some conversions or records saved together in one import), or an edit didn't touch a field in the matching rule.
Should Salesforce duplicate rules block or alert?
Alert people who type records in, so they can open the existing seller. Don't block records created by web forms, dialers or other integrations: a blocked record from an integration is a lost lead and nobody sees the error. Log every match to a report instead.
How many leads can I merge at once in Salesforce?
Up to three leads at a time. The person merging needs Delete permission on leads, so keep merging with ops or an admin.
Why did my Salesforce import fail with DUPLICATES_DETECTED?
An active duplicate rule matched records in your file. Imports can't show an alert to a person, so the rule can stop those records from being saved. De-duplicate the file against Salesforce before importing, or adjust the rule for imports.
Does Salesforce compare records in the same import with each other?
No. Records saved at the same time aren't compared with each other, so a file that contains the same seller twice creates two records. De-duplicate the file before you load it.
How should a CRM handle the same seller with two properties?
One person, separate deals or property records. Match the person on phone and email, and keep each property as its own deal so offers and closings don't get mixed up.
How do I find duplicates that are already in Salesforce?
Turn on reporting in your duplicate rules so new matches are logged, and run a report of leads grouped by a cleaned phone field to find existing ones. Clean them in weekly batches, starting with open leads.

## Which Salesforce Edition Do Real Estate Investors Need?
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-edition-real-estate-investors.html

Which Salesforce edition do real estate investors need?
Most real estate investing teams need Salesforce Enterprise , because it allows 200 custom objects for properties, offers and buyers, 2,000 active flows and API access for integrations. Professional can work for small teams that fit in 5 flows; Starter can’t hold property records at all. Here’s the comparison, from Salesforce’s own limits pages.
Starter allows 0 custom objects, so it can’t hold Property, Offer or Buyer records. Fine for a solo investor tracking contacts; not a wholesaling system. source
Professional / Pro Suite allows 50 custom objects but only 5 flows, and API access is an add-on for Professional (and shown as an add-on for Pro Suite on Salesforce’s pricing page), which many integrations need. source · source
Enterprise is where most growing investor teams land: 200 custom objects, 2,000 active flows, API included, approvals and joined reports. source
Don’t compare on list price. Most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive based on the business and number of users.
What can each Salesforce edition do for an investor?
 | Starter | Professional / Pro Suite | Enterprise | Unlimited
Custom objects (Property, Offer, Buyer) | 0 | 50 | 200 | 2,000
Custom fields per object | 25 | 100 | 500 | 800
Flows | Not listed | 5 | 4,000 (2,000 active) | 4,000 (2,000 active)
Active validation rules per object | 20 | 20 | 100 | 500
API access (needed by many integrations) | Not stated | Add-on | Included | Included
Flow Approval Processes | — | — | Yes | Yes
Joined reports | — | — | Yes | Yes
Custom report types | — | 50 | 300 | 2,000
Sales Engagement cadences | — | Extra cost | Extra cost | Included
Experience Cloud portals | — | — | Yes, licenses extra | Yes, licenses extra
Data Loader | — | Via API add-on | Yes | Yes
Sources: Starter · Pro Suite · Professional · Enterprise · Unlimited · API · API by edition · approvals · reports · Sales Engagement · Experience Cloud · import tools . Pro Suite and Professional allocations match on the pages read.
Which edition fits which investor?
Solo investor, a few deals a year
You may not need Salesforce at all. If you do, the question is whether you need Property and Offer records; if yes, Starter won’t do it. See do I need a CRM yet? and when Salesforce is overkill .
Small team, one market, few integrations
Professional or Pro Suite can work if 5 flows cover your automation and your phone and e-signature tools support it (DocuSign and RingCentral list Professional). Count your flows before you buy.
Team with acquisitions, dispo and VAs, several lead sources
Enterprise. You’ll want more than 5 flows within months, approvals for offers above MAO, joined reports, and API access for CallRail, Google Ads conversion import, Calendly or Aircall, which require it or Enterprise outright. CallRail · Calendly
Multiple markets or a fund with investor reporting
Enterprise or Unlimited, depending on volume, sandbox needs and whether Sales Engagement cadences are worth having included.
Why do Salesforce edition names keep changing?
Salesforce repackages often. In June 2025, Agentforce 1 editions replaced Einstein 1 editions. source Third-party reports say Salesforce introduced Core, Advanced and Max editions in September 2026, with existing customers keeping their edition; I couldn’t read Salesforce’s own announcement. Either way, map your needs to the limits above (custom objects, flows, API access) and ask your account executive which current edition delivers them.
Not sure? Answer nine questions in the free edition picker .
What does Salesforce cost for an investor?
I don’t publish list prices, because most businesses don’t pay them. After a conversation with a Salesforce account executive, many get a discount based on the business and the number of users. Get a quote for your exact user count and edition, then add the setup cost, before you compare with an investor CRM.
Questions
Which Salesforce edition is best for wholesalers?
Most wholesaling teams with several roles and lead sources fit Enterprise: 200 custom objects, 2,000 active flows and API access included. Professional can work for small teams if 5 flows and its integrations are enough.
Can Salesforce Starter track properties?
Not as separate records. Starter allows 0 custom objects, so you can’t add Property, Offer or Buyer objects.
Does Salesforce Professional include API access?
No. Salesforce says Professional can add API access as an add-on; it’s included by default in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer.
How many flows does Professional Edition allow?
Salesforce’s allocation page for Professional lists 5 flows, versus 4,000 total and 2,000 active in Enterprise and Unlimited.
Do investors pay Salesforce list price?
Most businesses don’t. A Salesforce account executive can offer a discount based on the business and number of users, so get a quote before comparing.

## 12 Salesforce Features Real Estate Investor Orgs Don't Use
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-features-real-estate-investors.html

12 Salesforce features your real estate org is probably not using.
Most investor teams on Salesforce use leads, opportunities, a few reports and a couple of flows. These 12 features are already in many of the editions you pay for, and each one closes a specific leak: duplicate sellers, missed calls, offers above MAO, profit nobody ties to a campaign. Each comes with the investor use case, setup in six lines, the edition (checked against Salesforce Help on October 20, 2026), a gotcha, and how to tell if your org already uses it.
Score your org as you read: under each feature, check your org the way it says, then tap "Using it" or "Not yet". Your score and your gaps show after feature 12, and nothing is sent anywhere. Prefer paper? Print the 2-page PDF checklist and hand it to your admin.
1. Scheduled paths in record-triggered flows
A flow that waits, then acts: 3 days after the last call, 2 days before a deadline.
Investor use case
Follow-up that runs for weeks and pushes itself back when a rep logs a new conversation. Also contract deadlines: a task to the coordinator 2 days before the inspection period ends.
Setup, in short
Add a "Last Contact Date" field on the Lead, stamped by a flow whenever a connected call or appointment is logged. Create a record-triggered flow on Lead (created or updated, only when the record is updated to meet the conditions). In the Start element, choose "Add Scheduled Paths" and create paths at 3, 14 and 45 days after Last Contact Date. On each path, create a follow-up task for the lead owner with the right script in the description. Add an entry condition so dead, converted or do-not-contact leads never get tasks. Test on 5 leads with back-dated contact dates before you activate.
Edition
All paid editions run flows, but Pro Suite allows 5 flows in total; Enterprise allows 2,000 active. Source
Gotcha
Changing the date field reschedules pending paths when the new date is in the future (good: a new call pushes the next follow-ups back). Paths that already ran don't fire again. $Record__Prior is not available inside scheduled paths, and a failed path retries a few times before it gives up, so check failed interviews in Setup.
Are you already using it?
Open Setup > Flows and your Lead flows. If none has a Scheduled Paths section in the Start element, you are not using it.
2. Matching and duplicate rules
Rules that catch the same seller before a second rep calls them.
Investor use case
Stacked lists bring the same owner in three times with different phone formats. A custom matching rule on phone, email and a cleaned property address stops the second record or flags it.
Setup, in short
Add a "Property Address Key" text field: street number + street name + zip, lowercase, no punctuation, filled by a flow. Setup > Matching Rules: new rule on Lead matching Phone (exact), Email (exact) or Property Address Key (exact). Activate the matching rule, then Setup > Duplicate Rules: new rule on Lead using it. Set the action to Allow, with Alert and Report on, while you test. Add a second rule comparing Leads against Contacts, so a past seller is caught too. After a week of duplicate reports, switch to Block where you trust the match.
Edition
Essentials, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited (Salesforce Help). Source
Gotcha
Rules do not run on lead conversion or manual merge. Up to 5 active duplicate rules per object. Imports and API loads that hit a blocking rule fail without a pop-up, so read the error file.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Duplicate Rules. If only the standard rules are active and nobody changed them, you are on defaults that do not know about property addresses.
3. Omni-Channel routing for leads
Push leads from a shared queue to the next available rep, by capacity and skill.
Investor use case
A shared seller-lead queue that hands each new lead to a rep who is online and under their limit, and can prefer the rep who covers that market.
Setup, in short
Create a Lead queue for new seller leads and add the acquisitions reps. Enable Omni-Channel in Setup; standard orgs now get Enhanced Omni-Channel. Create a service channel for Lead and presence statuses such as "Available for leads". Create a routing configuration (most available or least active) and set units of capacity per lead. Attach the routing configuration to the queue and add the Omni-Channel component to the sales app. Run a week with two reps before rolling out to the team.
Edition
Edition and licensing for lead routing are not stated on the Help pages checked; confirm with your Salesforce rep before you plan on it. Source
Gotcha
Routing happens once. If a field changes after a lead is routed, Omni-Channel does not re-route it. Standard Omni-Channel was retired in Summer '26 and orgs moved to Enhanced automatically.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Omni-Channel Settings. If it is off, or on with no routing configuration for Lead, you are not using it.
4. Custom notifications from Flow
A push alert on a rep's phone, sent by a flow.
Investor use case
Missed seller call: the lead owner gets a phone notification with the seller's name and a link to the record, and a callback task due in 10 minutes.
Setup, in short
Setup > Notification Builder > Custom Notifications: create "Missed seller call" with desktop and mobile on. Turn on mobile push for the Salesforce mobile app in Setup. Create a record-triggered flow on the call log (Task or your phone system's object) when the result is missed. Add a "Send Custom Notification" action with the lead owner as recipient and the lead as target. Create the callback task in the same flow. Test from a real phone with the Salesforce app installed.
Edition
Essentials, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited (Salesforce Help). Source
Gotcha
The limit is 10,000 notifications per org per hour, and extras are dropped, not queued. Mobile push has to be enabled separately.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Notification Builder. If the list of custom notification types is empty, you are not using it.
5. Path with guidance
The stage bar at the top of a record, with the fields and coaching for each stage.
Investor use case
At "Offer Made", the path shows ARV, repairs and MAO as key fields and a short checklist: comps logged, repairs walked, manager approval if above MAO.
Setup, in short
Setup > Path Settings > New Path. Pick Opportunity, the record type and the Stage picklist. For each stage, choose up to 5 key fields. Write the guidance: what must be true before this deal moves on. Activate the path; turn on celebrations for Closed only if your team likes them. Walk the team through one live deal.
Edition
Essentials, Group, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited (Salesforce Help). Lightning only. Source
Gotcha
Up to 5 key fields and 1,000 characters of guidance per step, and one path per object, record type and picklist.
Are you already using it?
Open any deal. If the stage bar has no "Key Fields" or "Guidance for Success" panel, the path is there but empty.
6. Dynamic Forms and Dynamic Actions
Fields and buttons that appear only when they matter.
Investor use case
Underwriting fields show once the appointment is set; contract fields only at Under Contract; the "Send to buyers" button only when the deal is ready for dispositions.
Setup, in short
Open the Opportunity record page in Lightning App Builder. Use the migration wizard to turn the page layout into field sections. Group fields into sections: Seller, Property, Underwriting, Contract, Dispositions. Set visibility on each section, for example Stage = Under Contract. In the Highlights Panel, enable Dynamic Actions and add visibility rules to buttons. Activate for the right app and profiles, then check on mobile.
Edition
Dynamic Forms: Group, Essentials, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited (Salesforce Help); Starter and Pro Suite not confirmed. Source
Gotcha
Not available on Tasks, Events, Products or Notes. Dynamic Actions work on desktop and mobile for custom objects but desktop only for standard objects like Opportunity.
Are you already using it?
Open the record page in Lightning App Builder. If you see one big "Record Detail" component, you are still on page layouts.
7. Screen flows for intake and offers
A guided form inside Salesforce that asks the questions and writes the records.
Investor use case
A seller intake script that captures motivation, timeline, condition and asking price, creates the Property record and calculates a draft MAO while the rep is still on the phone.
Setup, in short
New Flow > Screen Flow. Screen 1: seller and property questions, with picklists, not free text, where you report on the answer. Add an assignment that calculates a draft MAO from ARV, repairs and your target profit. Create or update the Lead and Property records. Add the flow to the Lead record page as a component or a quick action. New in Winter '27: screen flows can run in bulk from list views when the flow has an "ids" input collection.
Edition
Runs on the flow allowance of your edition (5 flows in total on Pro Suite). Source
Gotcha
Bulk launch from a list view needs a text collection input variable named "ids", or the button won't pass the selected records.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Flows, filter Type = Screen Flow. If the list is empty or only has sample flows, intake still happens in free text.
8. Field History Tracking and Setup Audit Trail
A log of who changed which field, and who changed the setup.
Investor use case
Settle the arguments: who reassigned the lead, who moved the stage back, who changed the lead source after the deal closed. Audit Trail shows who edited a flow before it broke.
Setup, in short
Object Manager > Opportunity > Fields & Relationships > Set History Tracking. Pick the fields that cause arguments: Stage, Owner, Lead Source, Campaign, Close Date. Currency fields like contract price can't be tracked, so lock contract price with a validation rule instead. Do the same on Lead: Owner, Status, Lead Source, Phone. Add the History related list to the record pages. Build an Opportunity Field History report for the Monday review. For setup changes: Setup > View Setup Audit Trail, download monthly.
Edition
Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited; Starter and Pro Suite allocations also list 20 tracked fields per object (Salesforce Help). Source · limits
Gotcha
Currency and percent fields can't be tracked. No history exists before you turn it on. The UI shows 18 months of history, the API 24. Setup Audit Trail downloads cover 180 days, then records are deleted.
Are you already using it?
Open a deal and look for a History related list. If it is missing or empty, nobody is tracking.
9. Joined reports and report subscriptions
Two reports side by side in one view, emailed on a schedule.
Investor use case
Campaign ROI on one page: campaign spend in one block, closed and kept-deal profit by the same campaign in the next. Subscribe the owner so it lands every Monday at 7 am.
Setup, in short
Reports > New Report > Campaigns, then switch the format to Joined. Block 1: Campaigns with Actual Cost, grouped by Campaign. Block 2: Opportunities with Campaign, filtered to Closed Won, summing actual profit. Add a cross-block formula: profit minus cost, divided by cost. Save to a shared folder and click Subscribe: Mondays, 7:00, owner and acquisitions manager. Put the same numbers on the Monday dashboard.
Edition
Joined reports: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer (Salesforce Help). Subscriptions: all editions, with 7 report and 7 dashboard subscriptions per user (15 each on Unlimited). Source
Gotcha
Joined reports can't use bucket fields, cross filters or conditional highlighting. The subscription cap is hard; support can't raise it. Dynamic dashboards can't be subscribed to.
Are you already using it?
Reports tab, filter by format. If you have no joined reports and nobody gets a Monday email, the owner is building ROI in a spreadsheet.
10. Flow approval processes
A built-in yes or no from a manager before a record can move on.
Investor use case
An offer above MAO, or an assignment fee below your floor, goes to the acquisitions manager for approval from their phone before the rep can send it.
Setup, in short
In Flow Builder, create an approval process flow (autolaunched or record-triggered) on Opportunity. Entry condition: Offer Amount greater than MAO. Approval step: approver is the acquisitions manager, or a queue if more than one person can approve. On approve, set Offer Approved = true; on reject, notify the rep with the comment. Add a validation rule so Stage can't move to Offer Made unless approved or under MAO. For autolaunched approvals, add the Request Approval component to the opportunity page; record-triggered ones start on their own.
Edition
Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer, Lightning only (Salesforce Help). Source
Gotcha
Classic approval processes still work, but new approvals should be built in Flow. Winter '27 allows up to 10 flow approvals on one record page.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Approval Processes and Setup > Flows. If neither has anything on Opportunity, offers above MAO are approved over text messages.
11. HTTP Callout in Flow with Named Credentials
Call another tool's API from a flow, without code or Zapier.
Investor use case
Send a new seller lead to your texting tool, or pull property facts from a data provider onto the Property record, inside Salesforce instead of a chain of Zaps.
Setup, in short
Get the vendor's API docs and an API key. Setup > Named Credentials: create an External Credential (holds the key) and a Named Credential (holds the URL). Give the right permission set access to the External Credential principal. In Flow Builder, add an Action > Create HTTP Callout, pick the Named Credential, set GET or POST and paste a sample response. Map the response fields to your record fields. Log failures to a field or a task so a broken key doesn't fail silently.
Edition
Generally available (GET since Summer '23, POST since Winter '24). Edition is not stated on the Help page; confirm with your Salesforce rep. Source
Gotcha
Editing an existing HTTP callout action or changing its Named Credential is still Beta. Schedule-triggered flows need a pause before a callout. Anyone with flow access can reuse the generated action.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Named Credentials. If it is empty and you pay for Zapier, there is probably a Zap that could be a flow.
12. Einstein Conversation Insights
Call transcripts, keyword tracking and call summaries on the records the calls belong to.
Investor use case
The acquisitions manager searches calls for "probate", "foreclosure" or "already got an offer" and coaches from real conversations instead of listening to everything.
Setup, in short
Confirm your phone system is a supported recording provider (some, like RingCentral, need extra setup). Setup > Einstein Conversation Insights: turn it on and connect the provider. Assign the Conversation Insights for Sales permission set to managers and reps. Add keyword trackers: motivation words, objections, competitor names. Add the call insights component to Lead and Opportunity pages. Review one week of calls with the team before you use it for scorecards.
Edition
Enterprise orgs can get up to 2,000 licenses at no cost with 60 processed call hours per license per year; generative call summaries are not available on Starter or Pro (Salesforce Help). Source
Gotcha
It doesn't record calls. It analyzes recordings from a connected provider, so no provider means no insights.
Are you already using it?
Setup > Einstein Conversation Insights. If it is off, the call recordings you already pay for are not searchable in Salesforce.
12 left to answer.
Close, but not in the 12
Kanban list views for a transactions board: up to 200 cards per view ( Help ).
Web-to-Lead takes 500 leads per 24 hours; extras wait in a queue ( Help ). Fine for most sites, not for a list upload.
Data Import Wizard vs Data Loader: the wizard handles up to 50,000 records, Data Loader up to 5 million and needs API access ( Help ).
Slack actions in Flow post hot-lead alerts to a channel once Salesforce and Slack are connected ( Help ).
Sales Engagement cadences are a paid add-on below Unlimited ( Salesforce ); ask your account manager for a quote; scheduled paths do most of the same job for free.
Salesforce Maps for driving for dollars and appointment routes: a paid add-on ( Maps ), included in Max ( Sales pricing ).
New to Salesforce? Start with Salesforce for real estate investors . Checking the basics first? Run the Deal Leak Score .
Questions
Which Salesforce edition do these features need?
Most work on Professional and Enterprise-level editions, but limits differ a lot. Pro Suite allows 5 flows in total, and joined reports and flow approvals are documented for Enterprise and above. Each feature above lists its edition with a link to the Salesforce Help page it came from.
Do I need a developer for any of these?
No. All 12 are configuration: Flow Builder, Lightning App Builder and Setup. You need someone who understands your process and has admin access, and a sandbox or test records before you switch anything on.
What should an investor team turn on first?
Duplicate rules and the missed-call notification. They are quick to set up and stop two common leaks: two reps calling the same seller, and voicemails nobody calls back.
Is there a printable version?
Yes. The REI feature checklist for Salesforce is a free 2-page PDF with all 12 features and a score box. On your phone, the Using it and Not yet buttons on this page do the same.
Feature names, editions and limits checked against help.salesforce.com, admin.salesforce.com and salesforce.com on October 20, 2026 (Winter '27 release). Salesforce Help still documents editions under the older names (Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited); in September 2026 Salesforce began selling Core, Advanced and Max. Salesforce is a trademark of Salesforce, Inc.; this page is independent.
Scored under 6?
That usually means the org was set up once and never revisited. I build and run Salesforce for home-buying companies. Book a 30-minute call and I'll walk through your org with you and point at the two features that would pay back fastest.

## Salesforce Features for Real Estate Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-features-real-estate.html

Salesforce features that matter for real estate investors.
For real estate investors, the Salesforce features that pay off are custom objects, Flow automation, validation rules, lead routing and reporting : they turn a contact list into a system that tracks every property, offer and buyer. Below are 37 features, what each does for a wholesaling or investing team, and the edition limits that decide whether you can use it.
The Salesforce features that matter most to investors aren’t the AI headlines. They’re custom objects (Property, Offer, Buyer), Flow automation, validation rules , assignment rules and reports .
Starter allows 0 custom objects , so it can’t hold a Property or Offer object. Professional allows 50 and only 5 flows; Enterprise allows 200 objects and 2,000 active flows. source · source · source
Each feature below has what it does, how a wholesaling or investing team uses it, and the edition or limit to know, linked to Salesforce’s own documentation.
Jump to: Data model Automation Routing Data quality Reporting Outreach Mobile Portals AI Security Import By edition
Can Salesforce model properties, offers and buyers?
Yes, with custom objects and relationships. This is the biggest difference from most investor CRMs, which give you a fixed lead-and-deal structure.
Custom objects
What it does: Your own record types with their own fields, layouts and reports. In real estate: A Property object (one record per address, however many times it’s marketed), an Offer object (every offer, not just the last one), a Buyer object with buy box fields. Edition / limit: Starter 0, Pro Suite and Professional 50, Enterprise 200, Unlimited 2,000. Custom fields per object: 25 / 100 / 100 / 500 / 800. source
Lookup and master-detail relationships
What it does: Link records. Master-detail deletes children with the parent and allows roll-ups; lookup doesn’t. In real estate: Offers as master-detail children of a Property, so “number of offers” and “highest offer” roll up. Seller as a lookup, because one seller can own several properties. Edition / limit: 2 master-detail and 40 total relationships per object. source
Junction objects
What it does: A many-to-many link built from two master-detail relationships. In real estate: Property ↔ Buyer: which buyers were sent which deal, who viewed it, who offered. That’s your dispo history. Edition / limit: Can carry roll-ups to both parents. source
Roll-up summary fields
What it does: Count, sum, min or max of child records on the parent. In real estate: Offers per property, total assignment fees per lead source, deals per buyer. Edition / limit: 25 per object by default, up to 40 via Support. source
Formula fields
What it does: Read-only fields calculated from other fields. In real estate: MAO = ARV × 70% − repairs. Assignment fee = buyer price − contract price. Days since last contact. Edition / limit: All editions; up to 3,900 characters. source · see the deal analyzer
What can Salesforce automate for a real estate team?
Flow (record-triggered)
What it does: Runs when a record is created, updated or deleted. In real estate: New lead → task for the assigned rep due in 5 minutes. Missed call → callback task. Stage = Under Contract → post to the dispo channel. Edition / limit: Professional and Pro Suite: 5 flows. Enterprise and Unlimited: 4,000 total, 2,000 active. source · Professional · Enterprise
Flow (schedule-triggered)
What it does: Runs at a set time and frequency on a batch of records. In real estate: Every morning: leads with no activity in 7 days get a follow-up task. Every Monday: stale offers flagged. Edition / limit: Same flow allocation as above. source
Screen flows
What it does: Guided forms with steps and logic. In real estate: A seller intake script that asks timeline, condition and reason, and only shows the asking-price question when the lead is hot. See the cold caller handoff checklist . Edition / limit: Same flow allocation. source
Flow Approval Processes
What it does: Multistep approvals where each step assigns a work item to a user, group or queue. In real estate: Offers above MAO, or above a dollar threshold, need the acquisitions manager’s approval before they go out. Edition / limit: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer; Lightning only. Salesforce calls it the modern alternative to classic approval processes. source · editions
More examples: 15 automation recipes for wholesalers .
How does Salesforce assign leads to the right rep?
Lead assignment rules
What it does: Ordered rule entries; the first match assigns the lead to a user or queue. In real estate: Leads from a market or zip code go to that market’s acquisitions rep; PPC leads go to the senior closer. Edition / limit: Up to 25 criteria per entry. source
Round robin
What it does: Salesforce’s documented method uses an autonumber field, a MOD formula and one assignment entry per rep. In real estate: Even split of inbound leads across 3 reps. Change the divisor when a rep joins or leaves. Edition / limit: Method from Salesforce Help. source
Queues
What it does: Shared buckets that team members claim records from. In real estate: A “Hot seller callbacks” queue anyone on the team can claim from when the owner is on another call. Edition / limit: No limit on the number of queues. source
Full setup: Salesforce lead and call routing for real estate teams .
How do you keep CRM data clean?
Validation rules
What it does: Block a save when the data breaks a rule you define, with your error message. In real estate: A warm or hot lead can’t be saved without timeline, reason and condition. A deal can’t move to Under Contract without a contract price. Edition / limit: Active rules per object: Professional 20, Enterprise 100, Unlimited 500. source · allocations
Four ways to require a field
What it does: Field-level (enforced everywhere, including imports), page layout (screen only), validation rule (conditional, everywhere), Dynamic Forms (that page only). In real estate: Use a validation rule for “required at this stage”. Use field-level only for fields every record has from day one, or imports will fail. Edition / limit: Salesforce Help comparison. source
Dynamic Forms
What it does: Show or hide fields based on record data, user or device. In real estate: Show the assignment fields only when exit type = assignment; show double close costs only for double closes. Edition / limit: Group, Essentials, Professional and up. source
Duplicate and matching rules
What it does: Block or alert when a new record matches an existing one. In real estate: The same seller arrives from a mailer, a web form and a list import. Match on phone and property address. Edition / limit: Up to 5 active duplicate rules per object. source
Path
What it does: A stage bar with key fields and guidance per stage. In real estate: Lead → Appointment → Offer → Under Contract → Assigned / Closed, with what the rep must capture at each step. Edition / limit: Up to 5 key fields and 1,000 characters of guidance per step. source
Kanban view
What it does: Drag-and-drop board of a list view, grouped and totaled. In real estate: Dispo pipeline by stage, summarized by expected assignment fee. Edition / limit: Essentials, Group, Professional and up; Lightning only. source
Field history tracking
What it does: Records old value, new value, who and when. In real estate: See who changed the lead source or the stage, and when. (Currency fields aren’t supported, so price changes need another approach.) Edition / limit: 20 fields per object; 18 months in the UI and 24 via the API without Field Audit Trail. source · retention
What reports can Salesforce build for investors?
Custom report types
What it does: Define which objects and fields a report can use. In real estate: Lead source → deal → assignment fee in one report, which is how you get cost per deal by source . Edition / limit: Professional 50, Enterprise 300, Unlimited 2,000. source
Joined reports and cross filters
What it does: Several report blocks side by side; filters like “leads without activities”. In real estate: Leads with no call in 7 days. Offers made vs contracts signed by rep, side by side. Edition / limit: Joined reports: Enterprise and up, 5 blocks. Cross filters: 3 per report. source
Reporting snapshots
What it does: Save report results to a custom object on a schedule. In real estate: Pipeline value every Monday, so you can chart the trend, not just today’s number. Pairs with the Monday 5 KPIs . Edition / limit: Professional and up; Professional allows 200. source
Dashboard subscriptions
What it does: Dashboards emailed on a schedule. In real estate: The owner gets the weekly numbers in their inbox without logging in. Edition / limit: Up to 500 recipients per subscription. source
Examples: 20 report recipes · pipeline dashboard · real estate KPIs in Salesforce .
Can Salesforce handle follow-up and email?
Web-to-Lead and auto-response rules
What it does: A website form creates a lead; an automatic email replies. In real estate: The “sell your house” form creates a lead with its campaign, and the seller gets a confirmation instantly. Edition / limit: 500 leads per 24 hours; one active lead auto-response rule. source · auto-response
List Email
What it does: Send a template to up to 200 leads or contacts at once. In real estate: A new-deal email to buyers in one zip code. Edition / limit: Counts toward the mass email limit, typically 5,000 recipients a day. source
Sales Engagement cadences
What it does: Sequences of calls, emails and tasks that appear in a rep’s work queue. In real estate: A seller follow-up cadence that runs for months, not days. Edition / limit: Included in Unlimited; extra cost in Professional and Enterprise. source
Einstein Activity Capture
What it does: Syncs email and calendar activity from Gmail or Microsoft to Salesforce. In real estate: Every email with a title company or buyer shows on the record. Edition / limit: Standard version in Starter through Enterprise; 6 months of activity stored. source
Does the Salesforce mobile app work in the field?
Offline and Offline Edit
What it does: Caches recent records and lets users create and edit offline; changes sync later. In real estate: Walkthrough notes in a basement with no signal; driving for dollars in rural areas. Edition / limit: Caches 30 recent records for each of 5 recent objects by default. source
Business card scan
What it does: Create contacts by scanning a card. In real estate: Meeting buyers and agents at a REIA meetup. Edition / limit: All editions except Database.com. source
Field workflow: driving for dollars with Salesforce .
Can buyers or partners log in?
Experience Cloud
What it does: External sites with Salesforce data and logins. In real estate: A cash buyer portal that shows available deals; a JV or bird-dog portal for submitting leads. Edition / limit: Enterprise and up; licenses bought separately. Partner Community is the license for lead and opportunity portals. source
Buyer side: wholesale dispositions in Salesforce .
What AI does Salesforce offer in 2026?
Agentforce sales agents
What it does: Agents for prospecting, lead engagement, pipeline management and coaching. In real estate: Agentforce Engagement can email-nurture cold seller leads; check consent and tone before you let anything write to sellers. Edition / limit: Usage-based credits; Agentforce Engagement needs Enterprise, Performance or Unlimited with Sales and Einstein for Sales. source
Einstein Conversation Insights
What it does: Analyzes recorded calls for keywords, mentions and next steps. In real estate: Flag calls where sellers mention foreclosure, probate or a deadline. Edition / limit: Listed for Starter, Pro, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Agentforce 1 Sales; connectors include RingCentral, Dialpad and Aircall. source
More: Salesforce AI and Agentforce for investors .
How do you control who sees what?
Permission sets
What it does: Add permissions on top of a profile; Salesforce’s recommended approach. In real estate: VAs can create leads but not see deal financials; dispo sees buyers but not seller notes. Edition / limit: All main editions. source
Sharing rules and field-level security
What it does: Open record access beyond defaults; hide specific fields. In real estate: Market teams see their own market; only owners see assignment fee fields. Edition / limit: Sharing rules: Professional and up, 300 per object. FLS: Professional and up. source · FLS
Multi-factor authentication
What it does: Required for all employee logins. In real estate: Matters when VAs log in from other countries. Plan it into onboarding. Edition / limit: Production enforcement rolled out July 20 to September 3, 2026. source
Role-by-role setup: Salesforce access for VAs and cold callers .
How do you get lists into Salesforce?
Data Import Wizard
What it does: Browser-based import for leads, contacts, accounts and custom objects. In real estate: A county list or a skip-traced list from PropStream. Edition / limit: Up to 50,000 records at a time; all editions except Personal and Database.com. source · tool comparison
Data Loader
What it does: Desktop tool for large imports, updates and exports. In real estate: Lists over 50,000 rows, or a full migration from Podio or another CRM. Edition / limit: Enterprise and up by default; uses the API, which is an add-on for Professional. source · API editions
Moving from another CRM: switching to Salesforce from Podio, REsimpli or GoHighLevel · moving off Podio .

Most businesses don’t pay list price: a Salesforce account executive can discount based on your business and number of users, so get a quote before comparing. Questions
What Salesforce features are most useful for real estate investors?
Custom objects for properties, offers and buyers; Flow for follow-up and missed-call tasks; validation rules so warm leads can’t be saved without key details; lead assignment rules; and reports that tie lead source to closed deals.
Can Salesforce calculate MAO?
Yes. A formula field can calculate MAO from ARV, your percentage and repair costs on every deal, so every rep uses the same math.
Is Salesforce Starter enough for a wholesaler?
Usually not. Starter allows 0 custom objects, so you can’t add Property, Offer or Buyer objects, and Salesforce doesn’t state API access for it on its pages.
How many flows does Salesforce Professional allow?
Salesforce’s Professional Edition allocation page lists 5 flows. Enterprise and Unlimited allow 4,000 total and 2,000 active.
Can I track who changed a lead’s stage in Salesforce?
Yes. Field history tracking records the old value, new value, user and time for up to 20 fields per object, kept 18 months in the interface without Field Audit Trail.
Does Salesforce work offline for driving for dollars?
The mobile app caches recent records and Offline Edit lets users create and edit records offline, syncing when the device reconnects.

## Salesforce for Real Estate Investors and Home-Buying Companies
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-for-real-estate-investors.html

Salesforce for real estate investors and home-buying companies.
Salesforce makes sense for an investor team when deals leak between steps nobody owns: missed calls, follow-ups that stop at touch two, offers made outside the system, and profit nobody ties back to the campaign that paid for the lead. This page shows how a home-buying operation maps into Salesforce, the ten builds that pay for themselves, what it really costs in 2026, and when you should not use it.
Who this is for, and who it isn't
I build and run Salesforce for US home-buying companies. For the last two years I have built and run the system behind a two-market home-buying company in Ohio, and for Pezon Properties, a property acquisition company in Pennsylvania, I built a campaign ROI dashboard and rebuilt their transaction coordination app. Everything on this page comes from that kind of work. I sell Salesforce work, so weigh my view with that in mind, and read the "not for you" list twice.
Salesforce fits when
You have about three or more people touching leads (acquisitions reps, a lead manager, dispositions, a transaction coordinator) and need to see who owns what.
You market in more than one channel or market and want profit per campaign, not leads per campaign.
Your process is yours: your stages, your underwriting, your rules. Investor CRMs are built around a typical process; Salesforce is built around yours.
You already pay for several tools that don't talk to each other, and someone rebuilds the Monday numbers by hand.
Salesforce is overkill when
You are a solo wholesaler or a team of two. An investor CRM or a clean spreadsheet will do more for less.
Nobody will own the system. Without an operations person or outside help, a Salesforce org decays faster than a simpler tool.
You want dialer, list stacking, skip tracing and mail in one box. REsimpli bundles those; Salesforce needs separate tools connected to it.
Your current tool already answers "who owns this lead, what happened last, what happens next" and your weekly numbers come out without a spreadsheet.
Not sure which side you're on? Score your funnel in two minutes with the Deal Leak Score .
What a home-buying operation looks like in Salesforce
A wholesaling or home-buying business is a chain of handoffs. Salesforce works when every link in the chain is a record with an owner, a stage and a date, and an automation that notices when it stalls.
Each step is a record someone owns and an automation that checks it. The dashed line is what most setups miss: closed profit written back to the campaign that paid for the lead.
Step | Lives on | Key fields | Automation that watches it
Marketing spend | Campaign | Channel, market, cost, dates | Spend entered monthly or synced from the vendor
Seller inquiry | Lead | Lead source, campaign, property address, motivation, owner | Duplicate rule, assignment to the shared queue
First conversation | Task and call log | Call result, duration, recording link | Missed call creates a callback task and an alert
Appointment | Event | Date, type (phone or in person), outcome | Stamps first-contact time for the speed-to-lead report
Underwriting | Opportunity + Property | ARV, repairs, desired profit, MAO, comps notes | MAO formula, intake screen flow
Offer | Opportunity (stage: Offer Made) | Offer amount, offer date, counter | Approval when the offer is above MAO
Under contract | Opportunity (stage: Under Contract) | Contract price (locked), contract date | Signed envelope updates the stage and alerts the coordinator
Dispositions | Buyer contacts + deal | Buy box: area, price band, type, rehab level | Matched buyer list; who was sent and who replied
Closing | Transaction | Title company, closing date, assignment fee or spread, actual profit | Transactions board; profit rolls back to the campaign
The free CRM field kit has these fields as CSV files you can import into any CRM, Salesforce or not.
The closing step has its own guide: transaction coordination in Salesforce . If nobody on the team owns the CRM after it's built, see hire an admin or use a retainer . Lending to investors instead of buying? See Salesforce for private and DSCR lenders .
If you renovate or keep rentals
Flips and rentals add two kinds of records to the chain above:
Renovation: linked to the property, with the scope, the contractor, budget against actual spend and milestone dates, so an over-budget job shows up before the sale instead of after it.
Partners and lenders: who put money into which deal and on what terms, with a scheduled report that sends each partner the status of their deals.
A house you keep is a return on the marketing that found it, so count it in campaign ROI alongside assignment fees. The Kept-Deal Map shows how.
The 10 builds that pay for themselves
These are the automations I'd build first for a team of 3 to 30. Each one closes a leak a reader can name. None of them needs code.
1. Missed-call alert
What it does
When a call from a seller number is logged as missed, Salesforce creates a callback task for the lead owner and pushes a notification to their phone.
Why it matters
A seller who reaches voicemail often calls the next buyer on the list, a point investors make in this BiggerPockets thread . This turns a missed call into a named job with a due time.
How it is built
A record-triggered flow on the Task (or the call-log object your phone system writes to) checks the call result. It creates a task due in minutes and fires a custom notification . Watch the limit: 10,000 notifications an hour per org, and Salesforce drops the extras rather than queueing them.
2. Shared lead queue
What it does
New seller leads land in a queue the whole acquisitions team can see, and the first rep to accept owns it.
Why it matters
Leads stop sitting in the inbox of the rep who is off today. Ownership is visible.
How it is built
A lead queue plus a lead assignment rule for web forms and imports. Bigger teams can route from the queue with Omni-Channel so reps get leads based on capacity. Only one lead assignment rule can be active at a time, so all routing logic lives in its entries.
3. Speed-to-lead clock
What it does
Each lead stores the minutes from created to first real conversation, by rep and by campaign.
Why it matters
You can't fix what you can't see, and without a field for it this number is a guess. See the speed to lead guide for why the first hour matters.
How it is built
A date-time field stamped by a flow when the first connected call or appointment is logged, and a formula field that turns it into minutes. A report groups it by owner and lead source.
4. Follow-up cadence that stops when the seller replies
What it does
Warm and cold sellers get dated follow-up tasks for weeks, and the cadence pauses when a conversation happens.
Why it matters
In my experience follow-up dies at touch two because nobody owns touch three. The cadence makes sure touch three and touch eight happen.
How it is built
A record-triggered flow with scheduled paths (for example day 3, day 14, day 45 after the last contact date). Changing the date reschedules the pending paths, so a new logged call pushes the next follow-ups back. Build your touch plan with the free cadence builder first.
5. Same seller, three lists
What it does
When a list import or a web form brings in an owner you already have, Salesforce flags it before a second rep starts calling.
Why it matters
Stacked lists repeat owners constantly. Two reps calling the same seller with two different offers costs the deal and your name.
How it is built
Matching and duplicate rules on the lead, matched on phone, email and a cleaned property address field. Gotcha: rules don't run on lead conversion or manual merge, and imports that hit a blocking rule fail silently, so check the import results file.
6. Campaign ROI on kept deals
What it does
Every closed deal carries the campaign that produced the first lead, and the report counts profit only from deals that closed or that you kept as rentals.
Why it matters
Cost per lead flatters the wrong channels. Cost per kept deal shows where to put next month's money. The Kept-Deal Map explains the idea.
How it is built
Lead source and campaign copy from the lead to the opportunity at conversion and lock after that. Actual profit lives on the closing record. A roll-up or flow sums profit back to the campaign, where campaign cost already sits. On Enterprise-level editions a joined report puts spend and profit side by side.
7. Underwriting on the opportunity
What it does
ARV, repair estimate, desired profit and the maximum allowable offer live on the deal, not in a side spreadsheet.
Why it matters
The offer and the math behind it stay together, so a manager can review the number and you can compare forecast with actual later.
How it is built
Currency fields for ARV and repairs, a formula for MAO (the same math as the free deal analyzer ), and a screen flow that walks the rep through intake questions. Lock the contract price when the stage moves to Under Contract.
8. Transactions board
What it does
Every deal under contract shows on a board by closing stage: title opened, inspection, buyer assigned, clear to close, closed.
Why it matters
Deals die between contract and closing when nobody calls the seller. A board makes the stuck ones obvious.
How it is built
A custom Transaction object with a stage picklist and a Kanban list view . Kanban shows up to 200 cards per view, so filter by market or closing month if you run more.
9. Buyer matching
What it does
When a deal is ready for dispositions, Salesforce lists the buyers whose buy box fits: area, price band, property type, rehab level.
Why it matters
Blasting every deal to the whole list burns buyers. Sending it to the ten who fit gets faster answers. The free cash buyers list template has the fields.
How it is built
Buy-box fields on the buyer Contact, and a flow or report that filters buyers against the deal's zip, price and type. Record who was sent the deal and who replied, so the list learns who really buys.
10. Signed contract alert
What it does
When the seller signs, the deal moves to Under Contract, the contract date is stamped and the team is told.
Why it matters
Nobody has to remember to update the stage, so the contract-to-first-call clock in your Monday numbers starts on time.
How it is built
An e-signature integration (I use DocuSign) writes the envelope status to Salesforce; a record-triggered flow updates the stage, stamps the date and notifies the transaction coordinator.
Edition matters: Pro Suite allows 5 flows in total ( Salesforce Help ), which is fewer than this list needs. Joined reports and approval processes are documented for Enterprise and above ( joined reports , approvals ). Already on Salesforce? See the 12 features most investor orgs don't use .
What it really costs
Licenses are the smallest part of the bill. Salesforce pricing depends on the edition and the number of users, and most businesses can get a discount through their Salesforce account manager, so get a quote for your team before you compare. What matters more is which edition your plan needs, because the limits below decide what you can build. In September 2026 Salesforce introduced Core, Advanced and Max and positions Core against the older Enterprise edition ( announcement ); Salesforce Help still documents limits under the older names.
Edition | What matters for an investor team
Starter Suite | No custom objects ( limits ), so no Property or Transaction records. Fine for trying Salesforce, not for running acquisitions to closing.
Pro Suite | 50 custom objects, but 5 flows in total ( limits ). API access is an add-on, and most phone and e-signature integrations need it, so ask for it in the quote.
Core | Salesforce's Enterprise-level edition. Help documents 2,000 active flows for Enterprise ( limits ), plus joined reports and approvals. Salesforce lists Premier Success and 500K Flex Credits a year with Core; confirm with your rep.
Advanced / Max | More AI, security and data tools; Max includes Salesforce Maps and Agentforce for Sales. Rarely needed under 30 users.
What goes into year one
Ask your Salesforce account manager to quote the edition your plan needs for your number of users, with API access if you connect a phone or e-signature tool. On top of the licenses come the build (scoped per project; my CRM Revenue Audit is a fixed $1,500 and ends with a roadmap you can build with anyone), your phone and texting provider, and whoever owns the system after launch.
For comparison, and to be fair to the other side: REsimpli lists its Team plan at $699 a month billed annually for 5 users, with dialer, list stacking and direct mail included ( REsimpli's own comparison , Oct 2026). GoHighLevel's Unlimited plan is $297 a month with unlimited users, plus usage fees for calls and texts ( GoHighLevel pricing ). If those tools answer your Monday questions, they are cheaper. Salesforce earns its cost when they can't. The switching guide has the full side-by-side.
Want to size the leak before the cost? The missed-call cost calculator and the cost per deal calculator take two minutes each.
A realistic timeline
This is the plan I'd propose to a 3 to 30 person team with one phone system and one e-signature tool. Data quality and the number of integrations move it more than anything else.
When | What happens | What the team feels
Weeks 1–2 | Audit the current tool, map every field, decide what history moves, agree on stages and owners | Two working sessions; nothing changes yet
Weeks 3–6 | Objects and fields, lead intake, shared queue, missed-call alert, duplicate rules, underwriting fields, phone sync | Reps test with real leads in a copy of the org
Weeks 7–8 | Import history, run both systems side by side, fix what the team finds | New leads go to Salesforce; old tool is read-only
Weeks 9–12 | Cadences, transactions board, buyer matching, campaign ROI and the Monday dashboard | Monday meeting runs from one dashboard
The five numbers to put on that dashboard are in the free Monday 5 . Already on Salesforce and not sure what's working? Check your Deal Leak Score , then the 12 features most investor orgs don't use .
Questions
Is Salesforce worth it for a real estate investor, or is it too expensive?
It is worth it when a team of roughly three or more people loses deals between steps and needs reporting its current tool can't give. License cost depends on the edition and the number of users, and most businesses can get a discount through their Salesforce account manager. In year one, the build and upkeep often cost more than the licenses. A solo wholesaler is usually better served by an investor CRM.
Which Salesforce edition should a wholesaler or home-buying company buy?
Starter Suite can't hold custom objects, so it can't store properties or transactions. Pro Suite works for a small team but caps you at 5 flows and leaves out joined reports and approvals. Teams that want the automations on this page usually need an Enterprise-level edition, which Salesforce now sells as Core. Check current limits with your Salesforce rep before you sign.
Can Salesforce replace REsimpli or Podio completely?
It can replace the CRM part: leads, deals, tasks, reporting and automation. List stacking, skip tracing, direct mail and the dialer come from separate tools connected to Salesforce. If you want all of that in one box with no admin, an investor CRM is the simpler choice.
Do I need a full-time Salesforce admin?
Not for a team of 3 to 30, but someone has to own it. That can be an operations person who handles small changes, with outside help for builds, or an ongoing management agreement. A Salesforce org nobody owns slowly fills with unused fields and broken automations.
How do sellers, properties and deals fit in Salesforce?
A seller inquiry starts as a Lead. When it becomes a real deal, it converts into an Account and Contact for the seller and an Opportunity for the deal. A custom Property object holds the address and property facts, so a repeat seller with a second house gets a second deal without a duplicate person. When to convert and what carries over: Lead, Opportunity or Property .
Does Salesforce have a dialer and texting for cold calling?
Calling and texting usually come from a connected phone system that logs calls and messages to Salesforce. I have built RingCentral call sync, and other dialers offer Salesforce integrations too. Calling and texting sellers is regulated: the FCC's telemarketing rules (TCPA) apply to calls and texts, and business texting follows carrier rules, including A2P 10DLC registration (see CTIA's messaging principles ). Check both with your provider and counsel.
How long does it take to set up Salesforce for a home-buying company?
It depends on how many tools you connect and how clean your data is. The plan on this page runs about 90 days from audit to full reporting, with the first useful pieces (lead intake, queue, missed-call alert) live in the first month. Treat that as a planning example, not a promise.
Can Salesforce show which marketing campaign produced each closed deal?
Yes, if the campaign travels from the lead to the opportunity at conversion and is locked after that, and if closed profit is recorded on the deal. Then a report shows profit per campaign against spend. Most setups break this chain at conversion or at closing.
What happens to my data if I leave Salesforce?
You can export your data as CSV files with the Data Export Service. Per Salesforce , weekly exports are available on Enterprise, Performance and Unlimited, and Professional-level orgs can export every 29 days. Data Loader can export larger sets where API access is included.
Can AI answer seller calls or write follow-ups in Salesforce?
Salesforce sells Agentforce for this ( Agentforce ). Pricing depends on how you use it and on your edition, so ask your Salesforce account manager for a quote. For most investor teams, the bigger win is fixing ownership and follow-up first; AI on top of a leaky process answers faster and still loses the deal.
Do I need a developer to set up Salesforce for real estate investing?
Not for most investor setups. Objects, fields, stages, automations built in Flow, and reports are point-and-click work. Code is usually only needed for an unusual integration, or a tool with no ready-made connector.
Can I move from Podio or REsimpli to Salesforce without losing my leads?
Yes, if you plan it: map every field first, keep lead source and created date on every record, merge duplicate sellers, and test 50 records before moving the rest. Podio's Excel export leaves out comments, files and tasks, so plan for those separately.

## Salesforce Integrations for Real Estate Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-integrations-real-estate.html

Salesforce integrations for real estate investors.
Salesforce connects to almost every tool investors use , including DocuSign, QuickBooks, RingCentral, Gmail, Facebook lead ads, Google Ads and Slack, through AppExchange packages, the API or tools like Zapier. Below: what each connection syncs, which edition it needs, and what it changes for a wholesaling team. Loading a PropStream or skip-traced list without duplicates: the import routine .
Most investor tools connect to Salesforce through an AppExchange package or the API. The API is on by default only in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer ; Professional needs an add-on. Check this first. source
The connections that change results most for wholesalers: phone and text logging , lead source capture , e-signature on the deal and accounting for assignment fees .
Open CTI, which many dialers use inside Salesforce, reaches end of life on February 28, 2028. Ask any dialer vendor what their plan is. source
Zapier and Make are fine for one-way hops. For two-way sync (accounting) or in-app features (click to dial, signing), use a native package.
Jump to: The matrix Before you connect Tool by tool Native or Zapier What to connect first Questions
Which tools connect to Salesforce, and what changes when they do?
One row per tool category an investor or wholesaling team typically runs. The “what changes” column is what I set up for real estate teams; the rest is from each vendor’s own documentation, linked under Sources.
Category | Connector (who builds it) | What syncs | Edition or requirement | What changes for a wholesaler | Deep dive
E-signature | Docusign eSignature for Salesforce (by Docusign) | Send from the record with fields merged into a template; signed PDF and signer data written back | Works on Professional and up, per Salesforce | Purchase and assignment contracts live on the deal; a signed contract can move the stage | DocuSign guide
Accounting | Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato (third party) | Invoices, payments and customers; direction depends on the connector | Ask the vendor; API access is likely to matter | Assignment fees invoiced from the deal; paid status visible in Salesforce | QuickBooks guide
Email and calendar | Gmail and Outlook integration, Einstein Activity Capture (by Salesforce) | Side panel logging; automatic contact and event sync | EAC Standard in Starter through Enterprise | Buyer and title emails land on the right record without copy-paste | —
Phone / dialer | RingCentral, Aircall, Dialpad, Twilio Flex, Salesforce Voice | Click to dial, screen pop, call logging, recordings | RingCentral: Professional+. Aircall and Dialpad: Enterprise or Unlimited | Calls per rep and contact rate per list without manual notes | Dialer guide
Texting | Dialpad or RingCentral SMS, SMS-Magic, Twilio for Salesforce (beta), Salesforce Messaging | Texts logged to the lead; opt-outs tracked | 10DLC registration required for app-to-person texting in the US | Seller texts in the same timeline as calls; STOP respected | Texting guide
Lead sources | Web-to-Lead, Lead Capture for Facebook, Google Ads Conversion Import, CallRail | New leads in; for Google Ads, contract stages back out as conversions | Web-to-Lead: 500 leads/day. Google Ads and CallRail need API access | Every lead has a source; ads optimize for contracts, not form fills | Lead sources guide
List data / skip tracing | PropStream export, BatchData API, BatchLeads via Zapier | Spreadsheet import, or custom API calls | No native Salesforce connector found for PropStream or BatchData | Skip-trace results and DNC flags written to the lead | —
Files | Files Connect (Google Drive, OneDrive, Box), Box for Salesforce | External files browsed and shared from Salesforce | Google Drive source: Professional and up | One folder per deal: photos, repair estimate, title, contracts | —
Team chat | Salesforce for Slack apps, Slack actions in Flow | Record alerts in channels; approvals in Slack | Salesforce Channels: Starter and up | #dispo gets the deal the minute it goes under contract | —
