Maps | Salesforce Maps (add-on), Geopointe (Ascent Cloud) | Leads and deals on a map; routes; radius search | Add-on; bundled in Agentforce 1 Sales | Driving-for-dollars routes from your own lead data | —
Email marketing | Account Engagement (Pardot); Mailchimp via Beaufort 12 | Two-way sync of prospects and email activity | Account Engagement: Professional and up | New-deal emails to buyers segmented by buy box; engagement on the contact | —
Glue | Zapier, Make, Workato | Trigger in one app, action in another | Zapier Salesforce is a premium app; API limits apply | Connects tools that have no native connector | Zapier guide
What do you need before connecting anything?
1. API access
Salesforce says API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer, and that Professional can add it as an add-on. CallRail, Calendly, Dialpad, Aircall and Google Ads all depend on it, and Calendly says Group and Professional editions “cause errors.” source · Calendly
2. A dedicated integration user
Each connection should log in as its own user with only the permissions it needs, so you can see what it changed and switch it off without breaking anything else. Salesforce offers an API-only Integration user license for system-to-system connections. source
3. Fields that the integration writes to
Decide where each value lands before you install: call outcome, lead source, GCLID, contract status, invoice status. If the field doesn’t exist, the data ends up in a note nobody reports on. The CRM field kit has the core list.
4. A test in a sandbox (when the connector supports it)
Google’s Salesforce conversion import does not support sandboxes, so test that one with a single campaign in production. source
5. Token limits
Zapier notes that Salesforce allows 5 access tokens per account across third-party apps, and a sixth silently revokes the oldest. Another reason to give each integration its own user. source
Tool by tool: what each integration does for an investor
DocuSign: contracts signed from the deal
Docusign’s own package sends agreements from Salesforce using templates that pull record fields through merge fields, and writes signed documents and signer data back to Salesforce. Salesforce lists it as working with Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Starter and Performance. For a wholesaler that means the purchase agreement and the assignment contract go out from the same deal record, and the signed copies stay there. source · Full DocuSign guide
QuickBooks: assignment fees you can report on
The common QuickBooks connectors are third party: Breadwinner and DBSync (packages) or Workato (integration platform). Breadwinner creates invoices from Opportunities, Accounts or custom objects and tracks paid, overdue and due status. DBSync maps Opportunity to Invoice, Sales Receipt or Credit Memo. Breadwinner · DBSync · Full QuickBooks guide
Gmail and Outlook: no more copy-pasting emails
Salesforce’s Gmail and Outlook integrations add a side panel to log emails and create records. Einstein Activity Capture syncs contacts and events automatically. Salesforce for Outlook, the old desktop plug-in, retires in December 2027. source
Dialers: every call on the lead
RingCentral supports Professional and above; Aircall and Dialpad require Enterprise or Unlimited. All log calls to Salesforce records. Several, including RingCentral and Twilio Flex, use Open CTI, which ends February 28, 2028, with Salesforce Voice as the recommended replacement. RingCentral · Aircall · Dialpad · Full dialer guide
Texting: compliant before it’s fast
Twilio states that anyone sending app-to-person texts over a 10DLC number to the US must register for A2P 10DLC. Salesforce’s own messaging retired its standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026, and US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks. Twilio · Salesforce · Full texting guide
Lead sources: every lead tagged where it came from
Web-to-Lead takes up to 500 leads a day from your website. Lead Capture imports Facebook lead forms (Professional and up). Google’s Conversion Import for Salesforce sends stage changes back to Google Ads, so ads optimize toward contracts. CallRail sends call data only; texts and form fills don’t reach Salesforce. Web-to-Lead · Facebook · Google Ads · CallRail · Full lead sources guide
PropStream and BatchData: lists and skip tracing
PropStream exports lead lists as a spreadsheet; I found no Salesforce integration on its pages. BatchData offers a skip tracing API that returns phones flagged mobile or landline, plus DNC and TCPA litigator checks, but no Salesforce connector, so connecting it is a custom callout or middleware job. PropStream · BatchData
Google Drive, OneDrive and Box: one folder per deal
Salesforce Files Connect lets users browse and share files from Google Drive, SharePoint/OneDrive and Box inside Salesforce. Box for Salesforce adds a Box folder on each record. Files Connect · Box
Slack: the team hears about contracts instantly
Salesforce builds the current Slack apps, including Sales Cloud for Slack, Approvals in Slack and Flow actions that post to channels. source
Calendly: walkthroughs booked onto the lead
The Calendly package creates or updates Salesforce records when someone books; if it can’t match an email it creates a new lead. It requires Enterprise or higher and a Calendly Teams plan or above. source
Salesforce Maps: driving for dollars from your own data
Plots records on a map with routes, territories and nearby search. It’s an add-on, bundled in Agentforce 1 Sales. source
Email marketing: buyer blasts that report back
Account Engagement syncs with Professional and higher every 2–4 minutes. Mailchimp’s current Salesforce integration is built by Beaufort 12. Account Engagement · Mailchimp
Native package or Zapier?
Need | Use | Why
Click to dial, embedded signing, a panel on the record | Native package | Zapier and Make don’t add anything inside the Salesforce screen
Two-way sync (invoices and payments) | Native package or Workato | Conflict handling and status updates both ways
“When a lead is tagged in tool X, create it in Salesforce” | Zapier or Make | Fast to set up for one-way hops
Near-instant reaction | Native package, or a Salesforce outbound message | Most Zapier Salesforce triggers are polling; the instant one is New Outbound Message
Zapier lists Salesforce as a premium app and says Salesforce API limits apply. source · common problems
What should a wholesaling team connect first?
1. Phone and text
Most seller conversations happen here. If calls and texts aren’t on the lead, nothing downstream (follow-up, reporting, coaching) works.
2. Lead sources
Web forms, Facebook, PPC and call tracking, each tagged with a source. Without this you can’t compute cost per deal .
3. E-signature
Contracts on the deal, and a signed contract moving the stage.
4. Accounting
Once deals close regularly: assignment fees invoiced from the deal, so reports show realized revenue.
5. Everything else
Slack alerts, maps, buyer email, scheduling. Useful, but they don’t fix a leak by themselves.
Questions
Does Salesforce integrate with DocuSign?
Yes. Docusign publishes Docusign eSignature for Salesforce on AppExchange. It sends agreements from Salesforce records using templates with merge fields and writes signed documents back. It needs a separate Docusign subscription.
Does Salesforce integrate with QuickBooks?
Yes, commonly through third-party connectors such as Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato, or through Zapier. They sync invoices, payments and customers between QuickBooks Online and Salesforce.
Which Salesforce edition do I need for integrations?
Many connectors need API access, which is included in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer, and is an add-on for Professional. Some, such as DocuSign and RingCentral, also work on Professional. Check each vendor’s requirements.
Can I connect PropStream to Salesforce?
I found no native PropStream integration with Salesforce. PropStream exports lists as spreadsheets, which you can import with the Data Import Wizard (up to 50,000 records at a time) or Data Loader.
What is happening to Open CTI?
Salesforce says Open CTI reaches end of life on February 28, 2028, and existing implementations stop working after that. Salesforce Voice is the recommended replacement. Dialer vendors that use Open CTI need a new path.
Is Zapier enough to connect my real estate tools to Salesforce?
For simple one-way steps, often yes. For two-way sync, in-app features like click to dial, or near-instant updates, a native package is usually the better fit.

## Get Every Real Estate Lead Source into Salesforce
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-lead-sources-real-estate.html

Every lead source into Salesforce, tagged.
Real estate investors get leads into Salesforce through Web-to-Lead for website forms, Lead Capture for Facebook lead ads, CallRail for calls, and imports for lists . Google Ads can then learn from which leads became contracts. Here’s each route, what it needs, and the rules that keep the source on the record to the closed deal. How to label sources, situations and campaigns without a mess: tags, fields or campaigns . Loading a purchased or skip-traced list: import without duplicates .
Web-to-Lead turns your website form into Salesforce leads, up to 500 a day. source
Lead Capture imports Facebook lead forms into Sales Cloud (Professional and up). source
Google Ads Conversion Import for Salesforce sends contract stages back to Google Ads, so ads learn which clicks became contracts. source
CallRail sends call data only; texts and form submissions don’t report to Salesforce. source
How does each lead source get into Salesforce?
Source | Route | What lands in Salesforce | Requirement
Website form | Web-to-Lead | A lead, optionally tied to a campaign; auto-response email | 500 leads per day; reCAPTCHA on by default
Facebook lead ads | Salesforce Lead Capture; or Meta’s partner integrations, webhooks or Zapier | A lead mapped from the lead form fields | Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited or Developer; admin on the Facebook Page
Google Ads | Web-to-Lead with a hidden GCLID field, then Conversion Import for Salesforce | The lead with its GCLID; later, stage changes go back to Google Ads | API enabled; GCLID field on Lead and Opportunity; field history on status/stage
Call tracking | CallRail integration | Calls with source, campaign, keywords, UTM, GCLID, recording, transcript; new leads when no match | REST API access
Lists (PropStream, county) | Spreadsheet → Data Import Wizard or Data Loader | Leads with list name as source | Wizard: 50,000 rows at a time
Sources: Web-to-Lead · Facebook import · Lead Capture requirements · Meta · Google Ads · setup · CallRail · CallRail fields · PropStream
Why connect Google Ads to Salesforce?
Without it, Google Ads optimizes toward form fills, and a tire-kicker counts the same as a motivated seller. With Conversion Import, you send “Under Contract” or “Closed” stage changes back as conversions, so bidding favors the keywords that produce contracts. Google’s requirements: the API enabled, a 255-character GCLID field on Lead and Opportunity mapped on conversion, field history tracking on lead status or opportunity stage, auto-tagging, and a hidden GCLID field on your form. Clicks older than 90 days aren’t imported, and the legacy integration lost support on May 31, 2025. source · legacy
Which stages to send, how to count phone calls and how to tell it’s working are in the Google Ads offline conversions guide .
What rules keep lead sources clean?
One picklist, set automatically
Lead source is a picklist, set by the form, the integration or the import, never typed. Free text breaks every report.
Source survives conversion
Map lead source and GCLID from Lead to the deal. If the source is lost at contract, cost per deal becomes a guess.
Duplicates merge, sources don’t vanish
The same seller from a mailer and a web form: keep the first source, record the second touch. Duplicate rules can alert or block.
Every new lead gets a task
A Flow assigns and creates a call task within minutes; see the speed to lead guide .
Questions
How do I get Facebook leads into Salesforce?
Salesforce Lead Capture can import Facebook lead forms into Sales Cloud on Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited and Developer editions. Meta also documents partner CRM integrations, webhooks and its Graph API.
Can Google Ads optimize for signed contracts from Salesforce?
Yes. Google Ads Conversion Import for Salesforce imports lead status or opportunity stage changes as conversions. It needs a GCLID field, field history tracking and API access.
Does CallRail send texts to Salesforce?
No. CallRail says text messages and form submissions don’t report to Salesforce; only call data does.
How many leads can Web-to-Lead capture?
Salesforce Help says up to 500 leads per 24 hours. Extra requests wait in a pending queue and you can ask Support for an increase.

## Salesforce for Private and DSCR Lenders: Loan Pipeline
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-private-lenders-dscr.html

Salesforce for private and DSCR lenders: the loan pipeline, borrower to payoff.
If you lend to investors, your borrowers are home-buying companies, flippers and landlords, and their deals move fast. Most small lending shops track that in a mix of email, a loan servicing tool and a spreadsheet of who's in the pipe. This page is how I'd lay out a private, hard money or DSCR lender's pipeline in Salesforce, using the same patterns I use for investor teams.
The data model
Keep it close to standard Salesforce objects so reports and integrations just work:
Thing | Salesforce object | Notes
Borrower company | Account | Most investor borrowers buy through an LLC; one account per entity, linked to the person behind it
Borrower, guarantor, broker | Contact | One person can be a guarantor on several entities; use contact roles
Loan request | Opportunity | One per property and loan; loan type as a record type (fix and flip, bridge, DSCR rental, construction)
Property | Custom object | Address, purchase price, ARV or value, rent for DSCR, linked to the loan
Conditions | Custom object or tasks | Each item you need before closing, with status and who owes it
Draws | Custom object | For rehab and construction loans: requested, inspected, approved, funded
Referral source | Campaign or field | Broker, mastermind, wholesaler, repeat, ads, so you know where good loans come from
Loan stages
Inquiry. Borrower or broker sends a deal. Speed matters here as much as it does for a wholesaler's seller lead. The borrower usually has other lenders on the same deal.
Term sheet sent. Rate, points, leverage and conditions out the door, with an expiry date.
Application and docs. Entity docs, track record, bank statements, insurance.
Underwriting. Valuation, title, the DSCR or leverage check.
Clear to close. Conditions met, closing scheduled.
Funded. Hand-off to servicing, whatever you use for it.
Paid off or refinanced. Close the loop and trigger the next conversation with the borrower.
Lost. With a reason: rate, speed, leverage, deal died, went with another lender.
"Lost, reason: speed" is the one to watch. If it shows up often, the fix is usually in the first two stages, not the rate.
Conditions and draws without the email chain
The slow part of most private loans is the list of things you're waiting for. Put each condition on the loan as its own line with an owner (borrower, title, insurance, you) and a due date. A Flow sends the borrower a reminder for anything they owe, and the loan officer sees one list instead of searching email.
Draws work the same way. Each draw request is a record: amount, line items, inspection date, approved amount, funded date. The borrower can submit through a simple form so the request lands in Salesforce instead of a text message.
Repeat borrowers are the business
A good investor borrower does several deals a year. The CRM should make the second loan easier than the first:
Track record on the account: deals done with you, on time or late, average loan size.
Documents on file with an expiry date (entity docs, insurance), so you only ask for what's out of date.
A task when a loan is a few weeks from maturity, to talk about payoff, extension or the next deal.
A simple tier for borrowers who close often and pay on time, so they get the fast lane.
It's the same idea as a wholesaler's VIP buyer tier in dispositions : the best repeat customers should get noticed automatically, not when someone remembers.
The reports a lending owner looks at
Pipeline by stage and expected funding date
Time from inquiry to term sheet, and from term sheet to funding
Lost loans by reason
Funded volume by referral source (which brokers and partners send loans that close)
Loans maturing in the next 60 days
Borrowers with expiring documents
For the DSCR math itself, the free DSCR calculator shows the ratio from rent and PITIA and the max loan at a target ratio. The same formula can live as a field on the property record.
Questions
Is Salesforce a good fit for a small private lender?
It fits when you have several people working loans, many repeat borrowers or referral partners, and you want reports on speed and source. A one-person shop doing a few loans a month is usually fine with something simpler.
Can Salesforce replace our loan servicing software?
Usually not, and it doesn't need to. Use Salesforce for the pipeline, borrowers, conditions and relationships, and hand funded loans to your servicing system. Sync the key status back if you want it in reports.
Can borrowers submit deals and draw requests straight into Salesforce?
Yes. A web form or an Experience Cloud page can create the loan request or draw record directly, so nothing gets retyped from email.
Do you work with lenders?
My main work is with home-buying and wholesaling companies, and lenders who serve them are a natural fit. If you're already on Salesforce, the CRM Revenue Audit works the same way; if not, start with a free call.
Lending to investors and already on Salesforce?
The CRM Revenue Audit (USD 1,500 fixed, for teams already on Salesforce) checks speed to term sheet, follow-up, data health and the reports you run the business on. On another system? We can scope a move to Salesforce on a free 30-minute call.
Or just ask one question about your setup: email · WhatsApp · LinkedIn

## QuickBooks + Salesforce for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-quickbooks-real-estate.html

QuickBooks + Salesforce for real estate investors.
QuickBooks Online connects to Salesforce through third-party connectors like Breadwinner, DBSync or Workato , which sync invoices, payments and customers. For investors, the payoff is assignment fees invoiced from the deal and paid status in Salesforce reports, so you see realized revenue and cost per deal by lead source.
The common QuickBooks connectors are third party: Breadwinner and DBSync (packages) or Workato and Zapier (integration platforms). Breadwinner · DBSync · Workato
For investors the point is realized revenue on the deal : the assignment fee invoiced from Salesforce, and paid status visible in Salesforce reports.
Mapping fees and marketing costs is a design decision. No connector does it out of the box.
Which QuickBooks connectors work with Salesforce?
Connector | Type | What syncs (per the vendor) | Notes
Breadwinner for QuickBooks | AppExchange package (third party) | Two-way sync of invoices and customers; invoice status (paid, overdue, due); payments; bills and purchase orders. Invoices can be created from Opportunities, Accounts, Orders or custom objects. | QuickBooks Online. One vendor screen calls QuickBooks data “read-only inside Salesforce”, so confirm direction per object.
DBSync | Package plus scheduler (third party) | Accounts/Contacts ↔ Customers, Products ↔ Items, Opportunity ↔ Invoice, Sales Receipt or Credit Memo; history migration | Sync by buttons or schedule. Opportunities need an Account and Standard Price Book products.
Workato | Integration platform | QuickBooks Online: 27 triggers, 87 actions. Salesforce: 16 triggers, 36 actions. | Most flexible; you design each recipe.
Zapier / Make | Integration platform | One-way “when X, do Y” steps | Good for simple hops; weaker for two-way accounting sync.
Sources: Breadwinner · DBSync · Workato . None of these pages states a minimum Salesforce edition; ask the vendor, and expect API access to matter. API editions
What should an investor track across Salesforce and QuickBooks?
Number | Lives in | Why it matters
Contract price, assignment price, assignment fee | Salesforce (deal) | The fee is a formula on the deal, so every report uses the same math
Invoice for the fee, paid date | QuickBooks, status synced to Salesforce | Separates fees you expect from fees you collected
Marketing spend by campaign | QuickBooks bills, totals pushed to Salesforce campaigns | Lets Salesforce compute cost per deal by source
Closing costs on double closes | Salesforce (deal) | What you actually kept; see double closing costs
Cancelled or renegotiated contracts | Salesforce (deal) | Fall-outs come out of campaign ROI
What does the flow look like for a wholesaler?
1. Deal closes in Salesforce
Stage moves to Closed. The assignment fee is already on the deal as a formula.
2. Invoice created
The connector creates a QuickBooks invoice to the end buyer or title company for the fee, from the deal.
3. Payment comes back
When QuickBooks shows it paid, the status updates on the deal. A “Closed – Paid” report shows realized fees by month and by lead source.
4. Spend meets revenue
Monthly marketing totals by campaign (mailers, PPC, skip tracing) land on Salesforce campaigns, and cost per deal becomes a report instead of a spreadsheet.
Questions
Does Salesforce integrate with QuickBooks Online?
Yes. The common routes are third-party connectors such as Breadwinner and DBSync, integration platforms such as Workato, or Zapier.
Can Salesforce create QuickBooks invoices from a deal?
Breadwinner says invoices can be created from Opportunities, Accounts, Orders or custom objects, and DBSync maps Opportunities to invoices, sales receipts or credit memos.
Should my accountant work in Salesforce?
No. Keep the books in QuickBooks. Sync only what Salesforce needs for reporting: invoice status, paid date and campaign spend totals.
Can I see profit per lead source in Salesforce?
Yes, if assignment fees live on the deal, the deal keeps its lead source, and marketing spend is recorded on campaigns. Then a report can show fees and cost per deal by source.

## Salesforce for Real Estate Investors: 50 Questions Answered
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-real-estate-faq.html

Salesforce for real estate investors: 50 questions, answered plainly
These are the questions that come up most when owners, ops leads and acquisitions managers at home-buying and wholesaling companies look at Salesforce. Each answer is short and leads with the answer itself. Where there's more to say, there's a link to a full guide. I run the Salesforce for a two-market home-buying company in Ohio, so the answers come from that work, not from a brochure.
Prices, limits and features below were checked in October 2026. Salesforce and other vendors change them, so check the linked guide or the vendor before you rely on a number. Nothing here is legal advice.
Is Salesforce right for your team?
Is Salesforce good for real estate investors and wholesalers?
Yes, for teams with a real process to run. Salesforce can hold every seller lead, call, offer, contract, buyer and closing in one place, with automations for follow-up and reports that tie marketing spend to closed deals. It isn't set up for investors out of the box, so it has to be built around how your team works, by someone like me or through an investor CRM built on Salesforce. More in Salesforce for real estate investors .
What size team should use Salesforce?
It usually starts to pay off at around 10 people, or sooner if you run several markets or spend heavily on marketing. Below that, an all-in-one investor CRM is often simpler and cheaper. Above it, missed leads and marketing you can't measure tend to cost more than the system.
Is Salesforce overkill for a solo wholesaler?
Usually, yes. A solo wholesaler or a team of two or three is better off with an investor CRM that bundles the dialer, texting and lists and needs no admin. Come back to Salesforce when you have reps, a second market or questions your tool can't answer.
Is Salesforce better than an investor CRM like REsimpli or Podio?
It depends on your size and how much control you want. Investor CRMs are faster to start and come with investor features built in. Salesforce takes more setup but lets you build your exact process, connect any tool and report on anything. I compare them in Salesforce vs investor CRMs and Salesforce vs Podio .
Do I need a special real estate version of Salesforce?
No. Most investor teams run on standard Salesforce with custom fields and objects for properties, offers and transactions. Some use an investor CRM built on Salesforce, which gives them a ready-made setup on the same platform. Either way, how it's set up matters more than which package you start from.
Which Salesforce edition does an investor team need?
Starter Suite can't hold custom objects, so it can't store properties or transactions. Pro Suite works for a small team but caps you at 5 flows in total and leaves out joined reports and approvals. Teams that want real automation usually need an Enterprise-level edition, which Salesforce now sells as Core. Confirm current limits with your Salesforce account executive before you buy.
Cost
How much does Salesforce cost for a real estate team?
It depends on the edition and the number of users, and licenses are usually the smallest part of the bill. I don't quote list prices because they change and they're negotiable: most businesses can get a discount through their Salesforce account executive, depending on the business and the number of users. Budget separately for setup and for someone to run it.
How much does it cost to set up Salesforce for an investor team?
Small-business implementations commonly cost $10,000 to $30,000, based on ranges a Salesforce consultancy published in October 2026. Where you land depends on integrations like the dialer, texting and accounting, how much data you move and how much automation you want on day one. See choosing a Salesforce consultant .
How much does a Salesforce admin cost?
In 2026, US median base pay for Salesforce admins is about $110,000 to $120,000 depending on the survey, with juniors around $78,000, according to Salesforce Ben's August 2026 roundup. Contract admins charge about $75 to $135 an hour. Details in hiring a Salesforce admin .
Can we get a discount on Salesforce licenses?
Often, yes. Ask your Salesforce account executive, especially at renewal or when you add users. Discounts depend on the business and the number of users, so get a quote for your real team instead of comparing list prices.
What does the CRM Revenue Audit cost?
USD 1,500, fixed, for teams already on Salesforce. If the report doesn't find at least five fixable issues worth more than the fee, you get a full refund. If you hire me for the build within 30 days of the walkthrough, the full fee comes off the project. See the CRM Revenue Audit .
Moving to Salesforce
How do we move from Podio to Salesforce?
Map what you track in Podio to Salesforce objects and fields, decide which history to bring, rebuild the automations that matter, then move every web form and phone number on one cutover day and check daily that no leads landed in the old system. Podio's Excel export leaves out comments and files, so plan those separately. The switch guide has the field map.
How long does a move to Salesforce take?
About 90 days for a typical investor team, with new leads flowing into Salesforce by around day 45, following the plan in my switch guide. Clean data and few integrations make it faster. Several tools and years of messy tags make it slower.
Will we lose call history and notes when we switch?
Some of it, often. Podio's Excel export leaves out comments and files, and other tools limit what they export. Move the history for open deals and active sellers, and keep the old account read-only for a few months for lookups.
Can we keep our dialer and texting tool if we move to Salesforce?
Usually, yes. Many teams keep their dialer and data vendors and connect them to Salesforce, so calls and texts land on the seller record. Check that the tool has a Salesforce integration and that your edition includes API access, which most integrations need.
What is Podio's new automation limit?
Since September 1, 2026, Podio Workflow Automation includes 25,000 actions a month. Extra capacity comes in prepaid, non-refundable add-ons on the Premium plan only. There's no automatic overage charge; automations above your capacity may be limited or fail instead. See Podio's new automation limit .
Can we keep GoHighLevel and add Salesforce?
Yes. Some teams keep GoHighLevel for marketing and texting and make Salesforce the record of every deal. Decide which system creates the person, sync on one key (usually the phone number) and add a duplicate rule on the Salesforce side.
Leads and speed to lead
How do I route leads automatically in Salesforce?
Use lead assignment rules to send leads to a rep or a queue based on things like market or source. Only one assignment rule can be active at a time, but it can have many entries, checked in order. Round robin and escalation take a little more setup. See lead and call routing .
Does Salesforce have round robin lead assignment?
Not as a simple built-in switch for leads. Common approaches are an auto-number field with a formula that cycles through values, paired with assignment rules; a Flow that picks the next rep; Omni-Channel routing; or an AppExchange app. The right one depends on your volume and whether rep availability matters.
How do I get missed-call alerts in Salesforce?
Connect your phone system so every call creates or updates the seller's record, then use a Flow to alert the rep or a Slack channel and create a callback task when a call is missed. It's one of the first things I'd set up for any investor team. See missed-call alerts in Salesforce .
How fast should we call back a seller lead?
As fast as you can, and measure it. In Harvard Business Review's 2011 study, firms that contacted a web lead within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify it as firms that waited even an hour longer. Most lead response research isn't about real estate, but it all points the same way. Sources in my lead response statistics .
How do I stop duplicate seller leads in Salesforce?
Set up matching and duplicate rules on phone, email and property address, decide whether to block or alert, and check what your web forms, dialer and imports create, because imports and API connections handle duplicate rules differently from manual entry. See duplicate sellers in Salesforce .
Can Salesforce stop texting a seller once they reply?
Yes, if your texting tool writes replies back to Salesforce. A Flow watches for an inbound reply and stops the cadence, so a seller who answered doesn't keep getting automated texts. Test it with a real reply before you trust it.
How do I know which marketing number a seller called?
Give each campaign its own tracking number and map each number to a lead source and market in Salesforce, so the lead is tagged the moment the call comes in. Then cost per contract by source works without anyone asking the seller where they heard about you. See lead sources in Salesforce .
Deals, contracts and dispositions
Can Salesforce calculate the maximum allowable offer?
Yes. Put ARV, the repair estimate, your fee and the offer percentage on the deal record, and a formula calculates the maximum offer, so every rep offers off the same math. The deal analyzer shows the calculation.
How do I track deals from contract to closing in Salesforce?
Give each stage the dates that matter (inspection, title, closing), create tasks for the transaction coordinator automatically at each stage, and run a report of deals missing a date. A board of every file under contract makes it visible to the whole team. See transaction coordination in Salesforce .
Can Salesforce manage our cash buyers list?
Yes. Store buyers with the zip codes and property types they buy, track what they've bought from you, and tier them by repeat purchases so your best buyers see deals first. Deal blasts can then go only to the buyers who match.
Can Salesforce send DocuSign contracts and track unsigned ones?
Yes, with DocuSign's Salesforce integration. Envelope status writes back to the deal, and a Flow can alert the rep or transaction coordinator when a contract sits unsigned for too long.
Can I track assignment fees and net profit per deal?
Yes. Record the assignment fee or resale price and the deal's costs on the closing record, then roll profit back to the campaign that produced the lead, so ROI counts only the deals that actually closed. See financial analytics in Salesforce .
Reports and numbers
What numbers should a wholesaling owner check every week?
I recommend five, which I call the Monday 5: cost per appointment by campaign, contracts per campaign, hours from contract to the first call back to the seller, booked vs. kept profit, and campaign ROI that includes the houses you keep. See the Monday 5 .
How do I see cost per contract by campaign in Salesforce?
Every lead needs a campaign or source, every campaign needs its monthly spend, and every deal needs a contract date. Then a report divides spend by contracts for each campaign. If source is blank on deals, check that your custom lead fields are mapped on conversion.
Why don't our Salesforce numbers match QuickBooks?
Usually because spend was entered differently from what accounting paid, reports count by different dates, or source and market get lost when leads convert. Reconcile one month, deal by deal, and agree on definitions. See why your Salesforce numbers don't match .
How do I track ROI by market?
Put a Market field on every lead, deal and campaign, filled automatically from the tracking number, form or zip code, and split spend the same way in your accounting. Then every report can be filtered or grouped by market. See the new market checklist .
Can Salesforce post daily numbers to Slack?
Yes. Once Salesforce is connected to Slack, a scheduled Flow can post a daily summary to a channel. I run daily numbers in Slack for the company I work with, so the team sees them without opening Salesforce.
Automation
Should we use Flow or Zapier?
Use Flow for anything that happens inside Salesforce: tasks, alerts, field updates, follow-up. Use Zapier to connect tools that have no Salesforce integration. Every Zap is another bill and another thing that can fail, and Zapier turns a Zap off automatically if 95% of its runs in the last seven days errored. At the company I work with, we moved Zaps into Flows after hitting the Zapier plan limit.
What happens when a Salesforce automation fails?
By default, Salesforce emails the person who last edited the flow. If that person has left, nobody hears about it. Send flow error emails to the Apex Exception Email list instead, with two people on it, and check the Automation app's Monitor tab for failed runs. See monitoring Salesforce automations .
Can our ops team turn notifications on and off without an admin?
Yes, if it's built that way. I build a configuration object, a settings record where ops can switch individual notifications and rules on or off without editing any automation. See the configuration object .
Do we need a developer, or can Flow do it?
Flow covers most of what investor teams need: tasks, alerts, assignments, field updates and simple integrations. Code makes sense for heavy logic or high volume, like syncing a full day of call logs from a phone system. Start with Flow and bring in code only when Flow hits a wall.
How many automations can we run in Salesforce?
It depends on your edition. Pro Suite allows 5 flows in total, which is fewer than most investor teams need, and Salesforce Help documents 2,000 active flows for Enterprise. Check the current limits for your edition before you plan a build.
Admin and team
Do we need a full-time Salesforce admin?
Usually not at 10 to 50 people. Most teams that size have a steady stream of changes, not 40 hours a week of them. A part-time or retainer admin who knows real estate covers it, as long as automations are checked monthly and changes are written down. See hire, freelancer or retainer .
What should we do when our Salesforce admin leaves?
Freeze their user, make sure someone still with you has admin access, then find everything that runs under their name: flow error emails, integrations, scheduled reports, records and queues. Move those, then deactivate. See the two-week handover plan .
Should we freeze or deactivate a user who left?
Freeze first, deactivate later. Freezing blocks login without changing anything they own. A frozen user still uses a license, so deactivate once their records and integrations have been moved.
How do we set up a new acquisitions rep in Salesforce?
Before day one: a user with a sales profile and a permission set, the dialer and texting connected to their own user, lead assignment that starts on their first calling day, three list views and approved templates. In week one, add a speed-to-lead alert that escalates to the manager. See adding acquisitions reps .
Can VAs use Salesforce safely?
Yes. Give them a restricted profile plus a permission set with only what they need, hide sensitive fields, and leave the export permission off so only owners can export your lead list. See VA access in Salesforce and stopping reps from exporting your seller list .
Compliance
Can Salesforce help with TCPA and Do Not Call compliance?
It can help you keep the records, but it doesn't make you compliant on its own. Track consent, opt-outs and Do Not Call status on the seller record, and stop automations when a seller opts out. TCPA damages are $500 per violation, up to $1,500 if willful, so have a lawyer review your process. This isn't legal advice.
How do we track wholesaling rules that differ by state?
Store the property's state on every deal and use it to pick the right contract template and required disclosures, with tasks that confirm they were sent. State rules change, so check them with a local attorney. See wholesaling laws and CRM tracking .

## 20 Salesforce Reports for Wholesalers (Recipes)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-reports-wholesalers.html

20 Salesforce reports for a wholesaling team.
The Salesforce reports that matter most to wholesalers show where leads come from, how fast they’re called, which offers become contracts, and what each source costs per closed deal. Here are 20 report recipes written as report type, filter, grouping and measure, the limits to know, and which five belong on the Monday dashboard.
These are 20 reports a wholesaling team can build in Salesforce, written as report type → filter → group by → measure , so you or your admin can build them in an afternoon.
Three features make them possible: custom report types (Property, Offer, Buyer), cross filters (“leads without activities”) and reporting snapshots (trends over time). source · snapshots
Most need fields that exist and are filled in: lead source as a picklist, call outcome, MAO, contract and assignment price, dead reason. Start with the CRM field kit .
20 reports for a wholesaling team
Report | Report type | Filter | Group by | Measure | Answers
Leads by source this month | Leads | Created date = this month | Lead source | Count | Monday 5
Speed to first contact | Leads with activities | Created last 30 days | Owner | Average minutes from created to first call (formula field) | Speed to lead
Leads with no activity in 7 days | Leads with or without activities (cross filter: without activities in 7 days) | Status not dead | Owner | Count | Follow-up
Missed inbound calls and callback time | Tasks / call logs | Direction inbound, outcome missed, last 7 days | Day, campaign | Count; avg callback minutes | Missed calls
Call outcomes by caller | Tasks | Type = call, last 7 days | Caller, outcome | Count | Coaching
Contact rate by list | Leads with activities | Source = list | List name | Contacted ÷ dialed (summary formula) | Lists
Appointments by campaign | Opportunities or events | Created this month | Campaign | Count; cost per appointment | Monday 5
Offers made vs contracts signed | Offers with deals (custom report type) | Offer date this month | Rep | Offers; contracts; ratio | Offer discipline
Offers above MAO | Offers | Offer amount > MAO (formula flag) | Rep | Count | Offer discipline
Pipeline by stage | Opportunities | Open | Stage | Count; expected fee | Pipeline
Days in stage | Opportunities with field history | Open | Stage | Average days (from stage history) | Bottlenecks
Contract to first TC call | Opportunities with activities | Under contract this month | TC | Average hours | Closing
Cost per closed deal by source | Campaigns with opportunities | Closed this quarter, fall-outs excluded | Lead source | Spend ÷ closed deals | Cost per deal
Booked vs realized fees | Opportunities | Closed this quarter | Month | Expected fee; actual fee; difference | Revenue
Fall-outs by reason | Opportunities | Stage = cancelled | Dead reason, source | Count | Honest ROI
Dead leads with re-contact date this week | Leads | Status = not now, re-contact date = this week | Owner | Count | Long follow-up
Days from contract to assignment | Opportunities | Assigned this quarter | Dispo rep | Average days | Dispo
Buyers who closed in 12 months | Buyers with deals (custom report type) | Closed in last 12 months | Buyer | Deals; total paid | Buyer list
Who changed lead source | Lead history | Field = lead source | User | Count | Data trust
Weekly pipeline trend | Reporting snapshot object | Last 12 weeks | Week | Pipeline value | Trend
What Salesforce report limits should you know?
Item | Limit
Rows shown in a report | 2,000 in the interface; export for more
Custom report types | Professional 50, Enterprise 300, Unlimited 2,000
Objects in one custom report type | Up to 60 object references, 1,000 fields
Joined reports | Enterprise and up, up to 5 blocks
Cross filters | Up to 3 per report
Dashboard components | Up to 25 per dashboard
Reporting snapshots | Professional and up; 200 in Professional
Field history | 20 fields per object, 18 months in the interface
Sources: limits · report types · joined reports · snapshots · field history
Which reports belong on the Monday dashboard?
Five, not twenty: leads by source, speed to first contact, offers vs contracts, cost per closed deal by source, and pipeline by stage. Everything else is for drilling in when a number moves. The reasoning and formulas are in the Monday 5 ; layout ideas in the pipeline dashboard guide .
Why do CRM reports get ignored?
Usually because nobody trusts the data. In Validity’s 2025 survey of 602 CRM users, 76% said less than half of their CRM data is accurate and complete. source The fix is upstream: picklists instead of free text, validation rules at each stage, lead source locked after creation, and a “who changed it” report so problems are visible.
Questions
What reports should a wholesaler run in Salesforce?
Start with leads by source, speed to first contact, leads with no activity in 7 days, offers vs contracts by rep, cost per closed deal by source and pipeline by stage.
How do I report on leads with no activity in Salesforce?
Use a cross filter: leads without activities, with a date condition such as the last 7 days. Salesforce allows up to 3 cross filters per report.
Can Salesforce show trends over time?
Yes. Reporting snapshots save a report’s results to a custom object on a schedule, so you can chart weekly pipeline or lead counts.
Why can I only see 2,000 rows in a Salesforce report?
The report interface shows up to 2,000 rows. Export the report to see all rows, or summarize with groupings.

## Texting Sellers from Salesforce: 10DLC and Consent
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-texting-real-estate.html

Texting sellers from Salesforce: 10DLC, consent and tools.
To text sellers from Salesforce in the US, you need a texting tool that logs to Salesforce, a registered 10DLC brand and campaign, and consent and opt-out fields every tool respects. Here are the tools, the registration steps, what CTIA’s guidelines say about lists, and how I set up the fields. This is not legal advice. Ready-made wording for each moment: seller follow-up message templates .
Twilio: “Anyone sending SMS/MMS messages over a 10DLC number from an application to the US must register for A2P 10DLC.” Registration has a brand and a campaign. source
CTIA’s guidelines say marketing texts need express written consent and senders “should not use rented, sold, or shared lists.” That matters for skip-traced lists. source
Salesforce retired its standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026; US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks. source
How can you text sellers from Salesforce?
Option | Built by | What it does | Watch out for
Dialpad or RingCentral | Dialer vendor | Texts from the dialer, logged to Salesforce | Dialpad logs SMS to the contact, not opportunities or shared lines
SMS-Magic Converse | SMS-Magic | Salesforce-native SMS, MMS, WhatsApp; templates, keyword auto-replies, campaigns, opt-in/opt-out tracking | Confirm current product naming with the vendor
Twilio for Salesforce | Twilio | 1:1 and bulk SMS from records; inbox component | Public beta, not covered by a Twilio SLA
Salesforce Messaging (enhanced SMS) | Salesforce | Native SMS channel in Service Cloud messaging | Standard channels retired Feb 14, 2026; registration takes 1–4 weeks
Sources: Dialpad · RingCentral · SMS-Magic · Twilio for Salesforce · Salesforce
What is 10DLC and do investors need it?
10DLC is the US system for business texting from regular 10-digit numbers. Twilio says anyone sending app-to-person texts over a 10DLC number to the US must register, including individuals. You register a brand (who is sending; standard brands need a business tax ID) and a campaign (the use case and your opt-in, opt-out and help messages). Registered traffic gets less filtering and more throughput. source
The Campaign Registry runs the registry behind it; brands register through a provider such as Twilio, not directly. source
What do the industry rules say about texting lists?
CTIA guidance (May 2023) | What it means for a wholesaler
Marketing messages need express written consent | A seller who filled out your form and agreed to texts is different from a number on a list
Honor STOP and plain-language opt-outs, one confirmation, then nothing | Opt-out must be a field in Salesforce that every texting tool respects
Don’t use rented, sold or shared lists | Bulk-texting a purchased or skip-traced list conflicts with this guidance
CTIA’s document is voluntary industry guidance, not a substitute for TCPA advice. Talk to a lawyer before you text lists. source
How should Salesforce store texting data?
Consent: a checkbox plus date and source (“web form, October 2026”). No consent, no marketing texts.
Opt-out: one field every tool checks before sending, set automatically when someone replies STOP.
Every text on the timeline: calls and texts in one history, so the next rep sees the whole conversation.
DNC and litigator flags from your skip-tracing provider, if it returns them. BatchData’s API returns DNC and TCPA litigator checks. source
Questions
Do I need 10DLC registration to text sellers?
Twilio says anyone sending app-to-person SMS over a 10DLC number to the US must register for A2P 10DLC. Toll-free numbers and short codes are separate systems.
Can I text a skip-traced list from Salesforce?
CTIA’s guidelines call for express written consent for marketing texts and say senders should not use rented, sold or shared lists. Get legal advice on the TCPA before texting lists.
What happened to Salesforce’s standard SMS channels?
Salesforce retired standard SMS channels on February 14, 2026. New channels are enhanced, and US long code registration takes 1–4 weeks.
Can texts and calls show in one Salesforce timeline?
Yes, if your dialer or texting tool logs both to the same record. Dialpad logs SMS as completed tasks on the contact; RingCentral logs calls and messages.

## Transaction Coordination in Salesforce for Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-transaction-coordination-real-estate.html

Transaction coordination in Salesforce: contract to close on one board.
The seller signed. Now title needs the contract, someone has to get the keys, the buyer wants a walkthrough and the closing date is three weeks out. In a lot of investor teams that part lives in a TC's head, a spreadsheet and a group text. This page is how I set it up in Salesforce instead: the stages, the fields, the automatic tasks and the one report the owner should look at.
Why deals leak after the contract
Most CRM effort goes into the front of the funnel: leads, calls, appointments, offers. Then the contract gets signed and the CRM goes quiet. The deal is "Under Contract" for three weeks, and the only way to know where it really stands is to ask the TC.
That's where the expensive problems are. A seller who doesn't hear from you for a week after signing starts taking other calls. Title is waiting on a document nobody knew they needed. The inspection window passes. In states with new wholesaling rules there are now cancellation windows and closing deadlines on top of that (see what your CRM has to track ).
Stages that match how a deal really closes
I keep transaction stages separate from acquisition stages. The acquisitions pipeline ends at a signed contract. The transaction picks up from there. A simple version:
Stage | Done when
Contract signed | Signed purchase agreement on file, closing date and title company set
Opened with title | Title has the contract and earnest money is sent
Due diligence | Inspection, walkthrough and photos done; repair estimate confirmed
Buyer secured | Assignment or second contract signed (wholesale), or financing confirmed (flip or rental)
Clear to close | Title commitment clear, closing scheduled with all parties
Closed | Funds received, file complete
Fell through | With a required reason, so you can see why deals die
Not every deal goes through every step. At Pezon Properties I rebuilt the TC app so the stages change by deal type, cash or financed, single-family or multi-unit, and the record only asks the questions that deal needs. That one change matters more than any dashboard: TCs stop skipping fields that don't apply.
The fields worth having
Dates: contract date, inspection deadline, cancellation deadline (where the state has one), expected close, actual close.
Parties: title company and contact, buyer, seller's preferred contact method, lender if any.
Money: purchase price, earnest money and where it sits, assignment fee or expected profit, closing costs.
Exit: assignment, double close, flip or keep as a rental. This is the field that makes campaign ROI honest later, because kept deals still came from a campaign.
Checklist: a short onboarding checklist for the property (keys, utilities, access, photos). Pezon's ended up with 40+ fields because they run several deal types; most teams need far fewer.
Last seller update: the date someone last told the seller where things stand. More on this below.
Tasks that create themselves
The point of all of this is that nobody has to remember. When a deal moves stage, Salesforce creates the next tasks, assigns them and dates them. A few that I'd always build:
Contract signed: send contract to title today, call the seller within 24 hours to explain next steps.
Opened with title: confirm earnest money received, schedule walkthrough.
Three days before the inspection or cancellation deadline: reminder to the TC and the acquisitions rep.
No seller update in 5 days: task to call the seller, and a flag on the board.
Clear to close: confirm closing time with seller, buyer and title; send the seller a plain checklist for closing day.
Closed: request the settlement statement, update profit and exit, ask for a review if it went well.
Fell through: reason required, then a task to put the lead back into follow-up if the seller still wants to sell.
Every one of those is a normal record-triggered Flow. No code. If your team changes the rules often, the Configuration Object approach lets ops change them without a developer.
One board for every file under contract
A Kanban view of transactions by stage, with the closing date, days in stage and last seller update on each card. That's it. At Central City Solutions every file under contract sits on one live Transactions Board, so nobody has to ask the TC where a deal stands.
Add a filter for "my deals" so each TC and rep sees their own, and a red flag for anything past a deadline or quiet for too long.
The TC scorecard
One report the owner looks at weekly. Keep it short:
Files under contract, by stage
Expected closings this month and next, with total expected profit
Deals past a deadline
Average days from contract to close, by exit type
Days since the seller last heard from you, worst first
Fell-through deals this month, by reason
The last two are the ones I'd watch first. When "days since seller update" is on a screen every week, people notice it.
Questions
Should transaction coordination be a separate object in Salesforce?
For most investor teams, yes, or at least a separate record type and stage set. Keeping acquisition stages and transaction stages apart makes both pipelines and their reports cleaner.
Can Salesforce track wholesaling law deadlines like cancellation windows?
Yes. Store the dates on the transaction and let a Flow create reminders before each deadline. It's a tracking setup, not legal advice; check the rules with an attorney in your state.
Do I need an app from AppExchange for this?
Usually not. Stages, a few fields, record-triggered Flows and a Kanban list view cover most teams. An app makes sense only if you need something specific like document generation.
We use a TC service outside the company. Does this still work?
Yes. Give the outside TC a limited user, or have them update a few fields through a form, so the owner still sees every file on one board.
Want your contract-to-close on one board?
I build transaction coordination in Salesforce as part of a full implementation, and the CRM Revenue Audit (USD 1,500, for teams already on Salesforce) checks whether deals under contract are tracked, dated and followed up. Start with a free 30-minute call.

## Salesforce Access for VAs and Cold Callers
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-va-access-real-estate.html

Salesforce access for VAs and cold callers.
Real estate teams can give VAs and cold callers exactly the Salesforce access they need with profiles, permission sets, sharing rules and field-level security, and protect the lead list by removing export rights. Here’s what each role should see, which features do it, and a VA onboarding and offboarding checklist.
Most investor teams have VAs and cold callers, often in other countries. Salesforce lets you give them exactly the access they need: permission sets , sharing rules and field-level security . permission sets
Salesforce enforces multi-factor authentication for all employee logins; production enforcement rolled out July 20 to September 3, 2026. Plan it into VA onboarding. source
Field history tracking shows who changed what, for up to 20 fields per object. source
What should each role see?
Role | Can | Can’t
Cold caller / VA | Create and edit leads in their queue; log calls; set outcome and next date | See deal financials, buyer list, exports, other markets
Acquisitions rep | Own leads and deals; make offers; send contracts | Change lead source after creation; delete records
Dispo rep | See under-contract deals and buyers; send deals; log buyer offers | See seller notes beyond what’s needed
Transaction coordinator | Closing tasks, documents, dates | Edit offer or assignment amounts
Owner / manager | Everything, including reports and fees | —
Which Salesforce security features do this?
Feature | What it does | Edition / limit
Profiles | Default settings for each user; one profile per user | Custom profiles in Professional and up
Permission sets and groups | Add permissions on top of a profile; Salesforce’s recommended approach | All main editions
Sharing rules | Open record access beyond org-wide defaults, by owner or criteria | Professional and up; up to 300 per object
Field-level security | Hide or make read-only specific fields, across UI, reports and API | Professional and up
Login IP ranges | Deny logins from outside set ranges | Per profile in Enterprise and up; Professional needs an add-on for per-profile ranges
MFA | Second factor for every employee login; phishing-resistant for admins | Enforced in 2026
Field history tracking | Who changed a field, from what, to what, when | 20 fields per object; 18 months in the UI
Sources: profiles · permission sets · sharing rules · field-level security · login IP ranges · MFA · field history
A VA onboarding and offboarding checklist
Before day one
Create the user with the caller profile and permission set; add to the right queue; confirm MFA method; share the call script and the handoff rules .
First week
Review their call outcomes daily; check the fields they skip; fix the layout before blaming the person.
Ongoing
Weekly calibration: compare their warm and hot leads with what acquisitions found.
Offboarding (same day)
Freeze then deactivate the user; reassign open leads and tasks to the queue; revoke integrations or dialer seats tied to them.
How do you protect your lead list?
Remove the export permission from caller and VA profiles; only owners export.
Give VAs list views, not report builder access, if they don’t need it.
Track changes to lead source, phone and owner with field history.
Keep integration users separate from people, so a departing VA can’t take an API connection with them. API access itself is included in Enterprise and an add-on for Professional. source
The other ways data can leave, and what you can see after the fact, are in stopping reps from exporting your seller list .
Questions
How do I give a VA limited access in Salesforce?
Give them a restricted profile plus a permission set with only what they need, hide sensitive fields with field-level security, and use queues and sharing rules so they see only their leads.
Does Salesforce require MFA for VAs?
Salesforce enforces multi-factor authentication for all employee logins, with production enforcement rolled out from July 20 to September 3, 2026.
Can I stop VAs exporting my leads?
Yes. Export is a permission; leave it off caller and VA profiles and permission sets so only owners can export.

## Salesforce vs GoHighLevel for Real Estate Investors
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-vs-gohighlevel.html

Salesforce vs GoHighLevel for investors.
GoHighLevel is a marketing platform with a CRM inside. Salesforce is a CRM platform you shape to your process. Neither has wholesaling data built in. Here’s how they compare, with every claim linked to the source.
GoHighLevel is a marketing platform: funnels, sites, texting, calling and workflows, billed by plan plus usage.
Salesforce is a CRM platform you configure: custom records, reporting, permissions and a large app marketplace.
Neither has wholesaling data (lists, skip tracing, cash buyers) built in. Both need a data tool next to them.
Disclosure: I build Salesforce CRMs for investors, so I have a bias. To keep it in check, every feature and price below comes from the vendor’s own site, linked in the row. I don’t list Salesforce prices: most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive based on the business and number of users.
Side by side
 | GoHighLevel | Salesforce
Built for | Agencies and small businesses; real estate page targets agents and brokerages source · real estate page | Businesses of any size source
Investor features | Property Investor bundle of templates, funnels and workflows source | None out of the box; you build Property, Offer and Buyer records
Calling and texting | Built in, usage-billed phone pricing | Add-on or AppExchange apps source
Funnels and sites | Built in | Not native; use your site and web-to-lead
Skip tracing and lists | Not built in | Not native; connect a data tool BatchLeads
Custom records | Custom objects source | Custom objects on Professional and up (Starter: custom fields only, 25 per object) source
Reports | Reporting; agent reporting on Agency Pro source | Custom reports and dashboards; field history tracking on chosen fields. Report recipes
API | Basic on Unlimited, Advanced on Agency Pro source | Enterprise and up; add-on for Professional source
Price | Starter $97, Unlimited $297, Agency Pro $497 a month plus usage. Published price, read from the vendor’s site in October 2026. Prices change; check the link. | Quoted. Most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive.
GoHighLevel’s usage fees
HighLevel bills phone and text by usage on top of the plan. Its help center lists US rates per minute and per text segment, plus A2P 10DLC registration and monthly campaign fees for texting. Budget for these at your volume, not just the plan price. HighLevel phone pricing
Where GoHighLevel wins
Marketing in one place. Funnels, sites, texting, email and calling in one tool.
Predictable plan price for the platform itself, with unlimited users on Starter.
Fast to launch if you use a template or snapshot.
Where Salesforce wins
Data model. A deal with several offers, a property with several sellers, a buyer with a buy box, each a related record with its own validation and automation.
Reporting and audit trail. Who changed the offer price, and when. 37 features investors use
Integrations. DocuSign, QuickBooks, dialers and data tools. Integrations guide
Governance. Sandboxes to test changes, permissions by team and market.
Running both
Some teams keep GoHighLevel for funnels and texting campaigns and send leads into Salesforce as the system of record. It works if you decide which system owns each field and sync only one way for most of them. Otherwise you get two versions of every seller.
Questions
Is GoHighLevel a good CRM for real estate investors?
It’s strong for funnels, texting and workflows. Skip tracing, list stacking and cash buyer search aren’t built in, and its real estate page targets agents and brokerages, so wholesalers usually add a data tool.
Is Salesforce better than GoHighLevel?
They solve different problems. GoHighLevel is a marketing platform; Salesforce is a CRM platform you configure. Salesforce is the better system of record when you need custom records, reports and permissions across a growing team.
How much does GoHighLevel cost?
HighLevel’s published plans in October 2026 are Starter $97, Unlimited $297 and Agency Pro $497 a month, with phone, text, email and AI billed by usage on top.
Can GoHighLevel and Salesforce work together?
Yes. One setup sends leads from GoHighLevel funnels into Salesforce. Decide which system owns each field before you connect them.

## Salesforce vs HubSpot for Real Estate Investors (2026)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-vs-hubspot-real-estate-investors.html

Salesforce vs HubSpot for real estate investors and wholesalers
HubSpot comes up a lot when investor teams outgrow spreadsheets or an all-in-one tool, usually because someone on the team used it at a previous job. It's a good CRM. The question is whether it fits a business where the records that matter are properties, offers, contracts and buyers, as well as contacts and deals. I build Salesforce for investor teams, so weigh my view with that in mind. I've tried to give HubSpot its due.
HubSpot is faster to set up and easier to run, and its prices are public. It fits a small, marketing-led team with a simple pipeline. The catch for investors is data structure: HubSpot's custom objects, which you'd want for properties, transactions and buyers, are an Enterprise feature. Salesforce takes more setup and needs someone to run it, but it lets you model the business as it is, automate deeply and report on anything. Around 10 people and up, with several markets or heavy reporting needs, Salesforce usually fits better.
Side by side
 | HubSpot Sales Hub | Salesforce
Built for | Sales and marketing teams of any size, contact and deal centered | Any business, configured to the process
Properties, transactions, buyers as their own records | Custom objects are Enterprise only, in any hub | Custom objects from Pro Suite up (Starter Suite has none)
Automation | Workflows: basic on Starter, 300 on Professional, 1,000 on Enterprise | Flow: 5 flows in total on Pro Suite; Salesforce Help documents 2,000 active flows on Enterprise
Reporting | No custom reports on Starter, 100 on Professional, 500 on Enterprise | Custom reports and dashboards; joined reports and approvals on Enterprise-level editions
Calling | Calling minutes included: 500 a month on Starter, 3,000 on Professional, 12,000 on Enterprise | Connect a dialer from the AppExchange or your phone system
Email sequences | Professional and Enterprise | Available through Salesforce features or apps, depending on edition
Ease of setup | Quick; most teams can set it up themselves | Needs someone to design and build it
Price | Per seat per month: Starter $9 annual or $15 monthly; Professional $90 annual or $100 monthly, plus $1,500 onboarding; Enterprise $150, plus $3,500 onboarding. Published by HubSpot, read in October 2026. | Quoted. Most businesses can get a discount from a Salesforce account executive.
HubSpot figures are from HubSpot's own Sales Hub pricing article and knowledge base. Salesforce limits are from Salesforce Help, as summarized in my Salesforce for real estate investors guide. Both change; check before you buy.
Where HubSpot wins
Speed to start. A small team can be working in HubSpot within days, without a consultant.
Ease of use. Reps tend to find it friendly, and adoption is easier when the tool feels simple.
Public, predictable pricing. You know the bill before you talk to anyone.
Marketing, if you're inbound-heavy. Teams that live on SEO, email nurture and landing pages get a lot from HubSpot's marketing side, which is priced separately.
Calling minutes included on paid Sales Hub tiers, which is enough for some teams' follow-up, though most wholesaling teams run a dedicated dialer anyway.
Where Salesforce wins
Your business, modeled as it is. A seller can have several properties, a property several offers, a deal one buyer and one closing. Salesforce handles that with custom objects from Pro Suite up. In HubSpot you either wait for Enterprise or squeeze it into contacts and deals.
Automation depth. Missed-call alerts, callback tasks, follow-up that stops when a seller replies, transaction tasks by stage, buyer matching. Flow handles all of it, with a lot of room on Enterprise-level editions.
Reporting. Cost per contract by campaign, ROI on kept deals, the owner's weekly numbers split by market. Custom report types and joined reports make the hard ones possible.
Integrations. Most dialers, texting tools, e-signature and accounting tools that investor teams use connect to Salesforce, and the AppExchange covers the rest.
Permissions. Fine control over who sees and edits what, which matters once you have VAs, several markets and a buyers list worth protecting.
Investor CRMs built on it. Some investor-focused CRMs run on Salesforce, so there's an investor-ready starting point on the same platform if you want one.
The cost question, honestly
HubSpot's price is public. For a made-up 10-seat team, Professional billed annually is 10 × $90 × 12 = $10,800 a year plus $1,500 onboarding, and Enterprise is 10 × $150 × 12 = $18,000 a year plus $3,500. Those are HubSpot's published per-seat prices; your real quote can differ.
Salesforce is quoted, and I don't publish list prices because they change and are negotiable. Most businesses can get a discount through their Salesforce account executive, depending on the business and the number of users. Salesforce also needs someone to set it up and run it, which is a real cost. I cover it in choosing a Salesforce consultant .
The fair comparison isn't Starter against Starter. It's the HubSpot tier that has what your plan needs (often Enterprise, for custom objects) against the Salesforce edition that has what your plan needs (often Enterprise-level, for automation). The edition picker helps with the Salesforce side.
Can you run both?
Yes. Some teams keep HubSpot for marketing email and landing pages and use Salesforce as the record of every seller and deal. HubSpot has a Salesforce integration for this. The rule that keeps it sane: decide which system creates the person and which owns each field, and sync on one key so you don't create duplicates. My duplicate sellers guide covers the Salesforce side.
If you're moving from HubSpot to Salesforce, the steps are the same as any move: map the fields, decide which history comes across, rebuild the automations that matter and cut over on one day. The switch guide has a field map and a 30-60-90 day plan.
How to choose
If this is you | Lean toward
Under 10 people, simple pipeline, inbound marketing is your main channel, no one to run a CRM | HubSpot (or an investor CRM)
You need properties, offers, transactions and buyers as separate records, and Enterprise HubSpot isn't in the budget | Salesforce
10 to 50 people, several lead sources and markets, owner wants cost per deal by campaign | Salesforce
Heavy cold calling and texting, with a dedicated dialer | Either; check the dialer's integration first
You already run HubSpot marketing and like it | Keep it for marketing; consider Salesforce as the deal system
Questions
Is HubSpot good for real estate investors?
For a small, marketing-led team with a simple pipeline, yes. It's quick to set up and easy to use. It gets harder when you need properties, transactions and buyers as separate records, because custom objects are an Enterprise feature in HubSpot.
Is Salesforce or HubSpot better for wholesaling?
For a team of roughly 10 or more with several lead sources, markets and a dispositions side, Salesforce usually fits better because it can model properties, offers, contracts and buyers and report across them. For a small team, HubSpot or an all-in-one investor CRM is simpler.
How much does HubSpot cost for a real estate team?
HubSpot's published Sales Hub prices per seat per month are $9 annual or $15 monthly on Starter, $90 annual or $100 monthly on Professional plus $1,500 onboarding, and $150 on Enterprise plus $3,500 onboarding, as of its September 2026 pricing article. Check HubSpot's pricing page before you buy.
Does HubSpot have custom objects for properties?
Only on Enterprise. HubSpot's knowledge base lists custom objects as an Enterprise feature in any hub, so on Starter or Professional properties have to live in deals or contacts.
Can I use HubSpot and Salesforce together?
Yes. Some teams keep HubSpot for marketing and use Salesforce for sellers and deals, connected through HubSpot's Salesforce integration. Decide which system creates each person and owns each field, and sync on one key to avoid duplicates.
How hard is it to move from HubSpot to Salesforce?
It's a normal CRM move: map fields, decide which history to bring, rebuild key automations and cut over all forms and numbers on one day. Plan for activity history that may not export cleanly, and run a small test import first.
Related guides
Sources
Checked in October 2026. HubSpot's own pricing article lists a few details inconsistently, and both vendors change plans often, so confirm on their pricing pages before you decide.

## Salesforce vs Investor CRMs (Podio, REsimpli and Others)
URL: https://amrmagdy.com/salesforce-vs-investor-crms.html

Salesforce vs investor CRMs: how far each one goes.
Investor CRMs like REsimpli come ready for wholesaling and are the faster start. Podio lets you build your own apps. Salesforce goes furthest on data model, automation, reporting and testing, but costs more and needs to be set up. The right pick depends on your team size, markets and the reports you need.
Side by side
What you need | Salesforce | Podio | Wholesaling CRMs
Built for wholesaling out of the box | No. You build the objects, stages and automations (or hire someone to). | No. You build your own apps. | Yes. Pipeline, stages and seller fields come ready.
Your own data model | Custom objects: 200 on Enterprise, 500 custom fields per object ( source , source ). | Custom apps built from field types, linked with relationship fields ( source ). | Custom fields on the built-in records; check the vendor for custom objects.
Automation | Flow: record-triggered, scheduled, screen and approval flows, built in ( source ). | Podio Workflow Automation, with plan limits on flows and monthly actions ( source ). | Drip sequences and task rules vary by product; ask for a demo of yours.
Reporting | Any field is reportable; joined reports (Enterprise and up) and reporting snapshots for trends ( source , source ). | Ask for a demo of the exact reports you need. | Ask for a demo of the exact reports you need.
Test changes before going live | Sandboxes: copies of your org for testing ( source ). | Not checked. | Not checked.
Calling and texting | Through AppExchange apps and integrations. | Not checked. | Often built in; REsimpli plans differ by calling and SMS minutes ( source ).
Price | Per-user monthly list prices, but most businesses get a discount from a Salesforce account executive based on the business and number of users. Plus setup. | See the vendor's pricing page. | See the vendor's pricing page.
Checked October 20, 2026 against each vendor's own pages. "Not checked" means I could not confirm it from an official page. Products change, so confirm in a demo.
How far Salesforce goes
Your process, not a fixed pipeline
One object for each thing you track: lead, property, offer, contract, buyer and assignment, all linked. Enterprise allows 200 custom objects and 500 custom fields per object, far more than an investor team needs.
Automation without code
Flow runs when a record changes (contract signed, so title and dispo get tasks), on a schedule (every Monday, "not ready" leads come back) and for approvals (an offer over MAO needs a manager). See the automations I'd build first .
Any question as a report
Cost per closed deal by lead source, offers over MAO by rep, days from first call to contract. Joined reports put marketing spend and closed deals in one view; reporting snapshots save the pipeline weekly so you see the trend. See the pipeline dashboard .
Built to grow
Sandboxes to test changes before they go live, field history on up to 20 fields per object ( source ), access by team and market, a daily API allowance that starts at 100,000 requests on Enterprise ( source ), and AppExchange, which lists more than 7,000 apps and consulting partners ( source ).
When Salesforce is overkill
Stay with an investor CRM if
You're solo or a small team doing a few deals a month, and the built-in pipeline fits how you work.
Salesforce makes sense when
You run several teams or markets, you need reports your tool can't build, or your process doesn't fit their pipeline. It should pay for itself in deals you keep, so get a quote first: most businesses are offered a discount on list price.
Questions
Is Salesforce better than an investor CRM?
Not for everyone. An investor CRM is built for wholesaling out of the box and is quicker to start. Salesforce fits when you have several teams or markets, need reports your current tool cannot build, or your process does not fit a fixed pipeline. I build on Salesforce, so weigh my view with that in mind.
How much does Salesforce cost for a small investor team?
Salesforce lists per-user monthly prices on its pricing page, but most businesses don't pay list. Talk to a Salesforce account executive: many teams are offered a discount based on the business and the number of users. Setup is extra, whether you do it yourself or hire someone.
Can Salesforce do what Podio does?
Podio lets you build custom apps from its field types and link apps with relationship fields. Salesforce does the same with custom objects and lookup fields, and adds built-in Flow automation, joined reports, reporting snapshots and sandboxes for testing changes.
Do I need a developer to run Salesforce?
Not for most investor setups. Objects, fields, page layouts, Flow automations and reports are built with point-and-click tools. Code is only needed for unusual integrations or logic.
What is the first step if I want to compare?
Write your stages from new lead to closed on paper, list the five reports you want every Monday, and ask each vendor to show you that exact flow and those reports in a demo.
